text: Prepare Flashbulb with alt fire before you Flow into the site, so it pops as you land, because the anchor dash has a windup in which you are as shootable as anyone and a flash that lands after you do is a flash for them.
when: a Hush entry that died in the dash
why: Flow is a delayed dash, not an instant one like Jett's

text: After the plant, steer Suspension onto the spike the moment the defuse starts rather than at the first retaker you see, because a lifted defuser is off the bomb and in the air for your whole team to shoot.
when: Hush holds her ultimate in a post plant
why: the ultimate levitates everyone it catches and it cannot be shot down

text: When a Hush anchor appears, aim at where the dash will land and not at where she stands, because Flow fires after a delay she cannot shorten and she is not protected while it winds up.
when: the player died to a Hush dash
why: untagged by agent so it can reach any agent, it competes on weight alone, and enemyHint keeps it from a known comp with no Hush

text: On Summit a dropped wall stays down for the whole round, so on defense wait for the hit to commit before you shoot the switch, because a wall dropped on a fake closes your own rotation and tells them which site is thin.
when: a defender on Summit before first contact
why: the three walls cannot be reopened once dropped

text: On Summit, time the wall drop with the entry so it cuts the defenders' sightline or rotation as you go in, because a dropped wall stays down for the round and blocks that line for the rest of it.
when: an attack on Summit dropped a wall before the hit
why: a wall is a free smoke that never fades, which is worth most in the seconds the entry is exposed

text: On Corrode walk through the water or take the dry route, because running through the flooded walkways splashes loud enough to call your lane, and on defense a splash with no footsteps under it still tells you exactly where they are.
when: any round on Corrode
why: the map has shallow water in its walkways that is audible at run speed

text: On Corrode take Mid Stairs with utility before you split a site, because a defender holding Mid Window from height sees the split form before it starts and A Link is reachable unseen only once mid is yours.
when: an attacker on Corrode planning a split
why: every guide and the Riot change notes put mid control first on this map

text: On Corrode two players with utility can hold B against a full execute, so do not stack a third there and leave mid and A Yard thin.
when: a Corrode defense that stacked B and lost A or mid
why: B is the compact defender sided site, the map guides make the two player hold its default

text: Recall Interceptor whenever its site goes quiet, because the reclaim comes back well inside a round now and a trap left on a dead site is a trap you do not have for the retake.
when: Veto whose site is not being hit
why: a patch cut the reclaim cooldown by a third

text: Fire your signature on the first contact rather than saving it for the site, because it comes back faster now and is up again by the time the hit starts, while information you held back is information nobody used.
when: an initiator holding the signature through the default
why: a patch cut the five signatures' cooldowns

text: Past 20 meters a head hit from your rifle leaves a full shield standing, so at a long angle land the head and keep firing for the next bullet instead of pausing on the hit, and inside 20 meters trust the one tap.
when: the player holds a Phantom and lost a long duel after landing a head hit
why: the far head hit is under the total of full health and Heavy Armor

text: On a pistol round a head hit from your pistol kills nobody who bought even Light Armor, so land the first head shot and keep tapping until they fall rather than stopping to see if it worked.
when: a pistol round duel lost after a head hit landed
why: the head hit is under the total of full health and Light Armor

text: Walking keeps you quiet but it does not make your rifle accurate, the first bullet still wanders off the head while you creep, so stop completely before the shot even when you were only walking.
when: a lost duel where the player was shift walking into the angle when they fired
why: rifle walking error is several times the standing error in Riot's own numbers

text: Inside close range hold the trigger, at mid range fire 3 or 4 bullets then step sideways and fire 3 or 4 more, and at long range tap single shots and let the gun settle, because the first bullets of a spray climb on one line you can pull down and the later ones jump sideways at random.
when: a rifle duel lost to a long spray
why: Riot protects the first bullets of a spray from a yaw switch, after that the spray can change direction

text: Make an information jiggle a single tap out and back, shorter than a holder can react to, because a holder needs about a fifth of a second to see you and fire, and a jiggle that lingers any longer becomes a duel on their terms.
when: the player died on what they meant as an information peek
why: exposure beyond human reaction time is a committed peek, whatever it was called

text: Spend one deathmatch moving your crosshair only sideways and never up or down, and count every time you had to flick down to a head, because each one is a spot where your resting crosshair is too high or too low and that count is what you are training to zero.
when: lost duels keep coming from low crosshair placement
why: the drill makes head height a habit and the count makes the habit measurable

text: Set a sensitivity where one comfortable swipe from the middle of your pad turns you about 180 degrees, then stop touching it, and when you must change it move it by about 5 percent for a miss that repeats and never after one bad game.
when: the player asks about aim or sensitivity, or overflicks repeat across matches
why: repeated overflicks mean too high, short flicks too low, and every change resets muscle memory

text: Run while the round is loud and switch to walking two corners before the spot you expect them, not at the last one, because running is heard through walls and the steps you took to reach the corner have already told the holder where to pre aim.
when: a death where the player ran up to the corner they died at
why: running is audible and walking is not, so the switch has to come before the information matters

text: Take height by jumping up, which makes no sound, and leave it by walking around rather than dropping, and swap guns, scope and pick up a weapon freely, because none of those is heard while a drop, a reload and a jump down to lower ground all are.
when: the player was found on or after leaving a perch, or asks about sound
why: players avoid silent actions and perform loud ones because they do not know which is which

text: If you keep having to flick at a wide swing, hold farther from the corner, because the player farther from the edge sees the other one first and a swing from distance arrives inside your crosshair instead of past it, and tuck in tighter only when your reaction is quick enough to win the flick.
when: a holder lost to a wide swing they saw but flicked past
why: distance from the dividing edge decides who sees whom first

text: Measure your entry by whether your teammates are on the site behind you a few seconds after your first contact, not by the kill, because a duelist who is still alone on site after the first fight has taken space nobody is using.

source.topic: entry is a four on five

when: the duelist's first kill or death comes with no teammate close and the team still outside the site
why: every coaching guide defines the entry as turning a five on five into a four on five that the team walks in on

text: In the buy phase tell your initiator which corner you want flashed or scanned first and swing on that pop, because a set piece agreed before the barrier drops lands on time and one improvised at the choke lands after you have already swung.

source.topic: agree the set piece in the buy

when: a duelist on a team with an initiator keeps dying on dry swings while initiator utility goes unused or lands late
why: the dry entry before the initiator's set piece is the most named duelist mistake from Gold to Diamond

text: When your drone, recon or the first contact shows three or more defenders on the site, call the rotate instead of entering, because an entry into a stack is a trade at best and finding the stack was the whole point of sending the scout.

source.topic: do not entry into a stack

when: the duelist dies to two or more defenders on a site a scout had already shown to be stacked
why: coaches list entering a stacked site among the times a duelist must not entry

text: Your flash blinds your own teammates as much as the holder, so when you flash for your own swing say it before it leaves your hand and throw it so it pops past the corner rather than in the lane your team is walking.
when: a flash agent duelist swings a corner while a teammate is in the same lane
why: Curveball, Blindside and Flashbulb all flash every player looking at them in the game's own text

text: If your entry dies before your flash or recon is out, do not step into their place, throw the utility you were holding for the player behind you and swing with them, because a second body through the same door without a set piece dies the same way.
when: an initiator dies at the same entrance seconds after the duelist, with a flash, stun or recon still unused
why: the coaching fix for a dead entry is to reflash at once for the next swinger

text: Count the defenders your scan showed and say where the rest must be, because two seen on the site means three are elsewhere, and that number is what your lurker and your flank watch need more than the positions you saw.
when: a recon, drone or knife count reveals part of the defence and a teammate is then killed from the side nobody called
why: coaches teach the count and the remainder together

text: Fire your recon as the team starts its last approach rather than once they are standing in the choke, because defenders move the moment they are revealed and a scan fired while your team is still a corridor away shows where they were.
when: a recon or drone is used well before the team is in position and the hit then meets defenders who have shifted
why: guides put the recon a couple of seconds ahead of the team's arrival

text: Pilot your drone or creature only from behind cover or a teammate and keep the flight short, because you are blind to your own body while you steer it and a defender who hears it deploy pushes you rather than it.
when: an initiator dies while piloting a drone or a creature from an open position
why: every piloted ability leaves the player stationary and defenceless

text: Aim Displacement at the wall beside the holder rather than at the holder, because the pull only concusses a player who is slammed into a surface or another player, and a clean pull into open air hands them a free turn onto you.
when: Hush pulls a defender and loses the duel that follows, with the defender never concussed
why: the game's own text says the concuss happens only on collision with a surface or a player

text: Prepare your flash and your pull with alt fire before you commit so your rifle is out when you turn the corner, and steer each one past the corner instead of throwing it blind, because a projectile redirected after the corner reaches a holder a thrown one never would.
when: Hush enters with her utility unprimed and either swings dry or is caught with a projectile in hand
why: Flashbulb and Displacement both read alt fire to prepare and reactivate to direct toward your crosshair

text: Do not stay in the air after an updraft, rise, take the one shot and land behind cover, because you cannot change direction up there and a floating head is the easiest shot on the map.
when: Jett dies mid air or just after landing from an updraft peek over a wall
why: guides list staying airborne after Updraft among Jett's common mistakes

text: Throw Leer above head height and off to the side of where the holder is looking, because an eye they can shoot without moving their crosshair dies before it nearsights anyone and a nearsighted holder is the duel your kit is built on.
when: Reyna's Leer is shot before the swing or placed in the holder's crosshair, and the duel is lost dry
why: Leer is destructible in the game's text and head level placement is why it is shot down before it works

text: Place your Run it Back marker behind a box or around a wall before the entry and move it to a new spot each time, because a defender who has seen the marker waits on it and kills you as you return.
when: Phoenix dies shortly after Run it Back returns him, or his marker sits in a lane the enemy has seen
why: Run it Back returns him to the marker at full health, so a seen marker turns the ultimate into a second death

text: Send Wingman to plant while you and your team hold the angles onto the spike, because the planter is the easiest kill of the round and the one body you can afford to lose is the little one.
when: a Gekko or a teammate dies on the plant while Wingman was available
why: Wingman's alt fire plants or defuses in the game's text

text: Cast your execute smokes as the entry starts moving so they land a moment before the first player steps onto the site, because a smoke thrown while the team is still gathering fades during the fight and tells the defence where you are going.
when: a controller's smokes went down long before the hit, or the entry walked in as they were fading
why: a smoke has a life, and the part of it that matters is the seconds the entry is exposed

text: On an execute, smoke the spots the defenders shoot from and leave your own doorway clear, because a smoke on the entrance hides their crossfire from you and you still have to walk out of it into every angle at once.

source.topic: execute smokes block angles not entrances

when: deaths stepping out of the team's own smoke on the choke, several angles firing at the exit
why: a deny smoke and an execute smoke are opposite shapes, one closes a doorway and the other closes the eyes watching it

text: On defence put your smoke a few steps in front of where you hold rather than on top of yourself, because a player who steps out of a smoke into your face has the first shot while one who has to cross open ground after it walks into yours.
when: a defender dies at point blank to an attacker emerging from the defender's own smoke
why: a smoke is a wall the attacker chooses when to cross, so the ground behind it must be yours, not your feet

text: Pair the smoke on a choke with a molly, slow or trap just behind it and keep that piece in hand until the push actually floods in, because a smoke alone only asks the push to walk through blind and the damage behind it is what makes them stop and wait for it to clear.
when: a site fell through a smoked choke with no delay bought, the rotators arrived after the plant
why: defence buys seconds, and a smoke buys them only when crossing it costs something

text: Hold a one way only from a spot where you can stand still behind cover, and leave it the moment it is sprayed or cleared, because a one way shows their feet once and after that the attackers know exactly which spot is watching.
when: a defender dies on a one way after its first kill or after the attackers started shooting through it
why: the one way is surprise, and surprise is spent on the first shot

text: Keep two setups for every site and switch after a round where they cleared your utility, because a trap they broke last round is a trap they walk around this round and the corner it covered is now the one they take.
when: the same trap or turret is destroyed in back to back rounds, the site falls the same way twice
why: a setup is information the attackers keep, so a repeated setup is a map of what you cannot see

text: Layer your utility at different depths, one piece at the entrance, one halfway in and one on the site, because a single line of traps tells them the site is clear the moment they are past it.
when: all of a sentinel's utility sat on the choke, the attackers walked onto the site freely once through it
why: delay is bought in stages, and every stage is another call to the rotators

text: Leave your site only once your team has seen three or more attackers at the other one, and leave a piece of your setup behind that still watches your entrance, because a single footstep is the cheapest fake there is and a site with nothing on it is taken in silence.

source.topic: rotate on a count, not a sound

when: a sentinel rotated off the first noise and the attackers planted on the empty site, or died mid rotation
why: the sentinel is the last to leave by design, because their utility is the site's memory while they are gone

text: Call the push the moment your first piece of utility triggers and keep delaying from behind the rest rather than peeking it, because the rotators need about the time one trap and one fall back buys, and a dead anchor buys nothing.
when: the anchor died early in the choke before any call, the site was lost before the rotation started
why: an anchor's round is measured in seconds, a trade for a trade with a call is a won retake

text: Place your flank trap behind the team as soon as the first piece of ground is taken, not when the hit starts, because a late flank watch is no flank watch and the defender walking in behind arrives while you are still planting.
when: a sentinel on attack dies, or a teammate does, to a defender who came through ground the team had already taken
why: ground you took and stopped watching belongs to whoever walks through it next

text: If your team is losing the first fights on the main side, stop lurking and join them, because a lurk only pays against a defence that is busy, and a defence that just won its duels is free to come and find you.
when: a lurker dies alone after two or more teammates already fell on the other side of the map
why: the lurk is a bet on the defence being pulled, and once the pull has failed the bet is off

text: On Abyss, commit to one site when you rotate rather than drifting halfway through mid, because mid is open ground watched from both ends and a half rotation gets shot from the side it did not pick.
when: a defender on Abyss died in mid between the two sites
why: the map guides name the half rotation through mid as the death that keeps repeating on Abyss

text: On Bind, keep a trap or a crosshair on the teleporter exit on your side whenever the other site is loud, because the split through the teleporter is how a hit on one site becomes a plant on yours.
when: a Bind defender lost the quiet site to attackers who arrived through the teleporter
why: the teleporters are the map's only fast rotate and the guides list ignoring the exit as the first Bind mistake

text: On Haven, the B anchor holds the cross between Mid Window and B Back and calls the push rather than fighting it, because B is the site both rotators reach fastest and a live anchor makes it a three player retake.
when: the Haven B holder died fighting the hit at the entrance before anyone rotated
why: B is the smallest site and the one the rotations reach first, so the anchor's job is the call

text: On Lotus, break the A wall only as part of a hit you are about to run, because it stays broken all round and an early break hands the defenders a new angle on A Main for free.
when: an attack on Lotus broke the wall early and the A hit later died to the angle it opened
why: the broken wall is a one way change to the map and the guides name an early break as a Lotus mistake

text: On Sunset clear A Elbow or B Market before you commit onto a site, because a hit through main with the connector unchecked gets shot from behind by the player who was watching mid.
when: an attacker on Sunset died on site to a defender coming from the connector
why: the two connectors join mid to each site, so a mid player reaches the back of either hit

text: Call the count first, then the place, then what they are doing, as in two A main pushing, and say at least two when you are not sure, because the count is what tells your team whether to rotate and a guess sends them the wrong way.
when: the player's calls name a place without a number, or give a number they did not see
why: comms guides teach count, location, state, count first because the listener decides the rotate on it

text: Make one position call within three seconds of dying and then go quiet apart from spent utility and credits you can see while spectating, because the survivors need the footsteps you are talking over more than they need your story.
when: a review round where the player died early and the round was still live for a while
why: one final position call, then silence, chatter blocks audio cues

text: Answer a rotate or site call with one word and move, and keep your disagreement for after the round, because a team that argues for five seconds arrives at the fight after it is over.
when: a round where the team split between two sites or arrived to a retake one at a time
why: confirm with one word, disagreements wait for the debrief, never criticise mid round

text: Keep each call to about three seconds and make only a handful a round, and never narrate your own duel or reload, because continuous talk covers the footstep and ability sounds your teammates need to swing on.
when: a player whose calls are long or constant, which the review cannot see directly, so this serves as general active round advice
why: about three seconds a call, a few bursts a round, mute after your call

text: When contact starts, listen for a full second before you speak, because the footsteps and the utility sounds in that second tell you how many are there and a call shouted over them tells the team nothing new.
when: a round lost to a misread of numbers or a rotate called on a first sound
why: the first second of a mid round contact is listening, hear footsteps and utility, register positions, then speak

text: Follow your entry about five meters behind on a different line, close enough to shoot their killer within a second or two and far enough that one flash or one spray does not take you both, because a trade that arrives after the killer has reset is not a trade.
when: an entry's death that nobody traded, or a second player who died to the same utility as the first
why: spacing lessons give about five meters and the trackers give a few seconds for the killer to die

text: If you are losing a fight, lose it moving toward your team rather than backing out alone, because a death taken while entering with a teammate behind you gets traded and a death taken while retreating almost never does.
when: a death while retreating from a lost fight with no trade
why: trade statistics show deaths while entering with teammates behind are usually traded and deaths while retreating rarely are

text: With two duelists on the team, settle in the buy phase who enters first and who trades, because two players who both think they are the entry swing into the same angle together and two who both think they are the trade leave nobody in front.
when: a double duelist comp where the player's first death was alongside or behind the other duelist
why: in a double duelist comp decide in advance who enters first and who trades

text: Make the buy call before the site call, then change the plan at most once in the round, because a second change mid round leaves five players in five places with their utility already spent on the first plan.
when: a round where the team rotated twice or re planned after utility was gone
why: economy check first, then the comp call, then utility and ultimates, and only a single mid round adjustment

text: After a death, take one slow breath on the death screen and turn the verdict into an instruction, not I am bad but I swung without clearing so next round I clear first, because an instruction changes the next round and a verdict only changes your mood.
when: a deathstreak pattern
why: one deliberate breath after a death, turn verdicts into instructions, anger is the strongest predictor of tilt

text: After a lost round say one short supportive line and nothing about who was wrong, because the first seconds after a round are when a bad mood spreads to the team and criticism there costs the next round as well.
when: a run of lost rounds, the streak pattern
why: be supportive right after a thrown or narrow round, do not dwell, negativity spreads quickly

text: Stop queueing after two losses in a row and take at least fifteen minutes away from the screen, because tilt carried into a third match tends to play worse than the first two and a short break is the simplest reset there is.
when: a match lost after another loss, which the review cannot see today, so the deathstreak tag is the nearest hook
why: two losses means a break, the common ranked rule against playing tilted

text: After you win the pistol, carry the cheap gun you bought into the third round instead of upgrading to a rifle, because that round is your bonus and a lost bonus with a saved rifle budget still leaves you a full buy while an upgraded rifle lost there does not.
when: buy phase of round three or fifteen with the pistol and the second round won
why: every economy guide names round three after two wins as the bonus, the existing bonus round note says how to play it and not what to buy

text: On the last round of a half and on the round before overtime, spend every credit you have, because nothing carries over the side swap and a bank you did not spend is a free round handed to them.
when: buy phase of the last round of a half in a standard match
why: credits reset at the half and overtime starts everyone fresh, so the usual save logic is void

text: When you are the only one who can afford a rifle, buy what the four others are buying instead, because a lone rifle on a save round dies alone, hands them a free gun and leaves you short for the real buy.

source.topic: no solo buy on a team save

when: the player's credits are far above the team's during a save or force
why: the existing buy with your team note covers the team rule, this one covers the richest player's temptation

text: If you are on attack and the round is lost with no plant, or on defense and the spike will go off, and all you hold is a sidearm, do not hide to survive, because a survivor in those two cases is paid 1000 credits instead of the loss bonus and a sidearm is worth less than the difference.
when: last alive on a lost round with only a sidearm, an attacker with no plant or a defender before detonation
why: Riot's patch notes 1.11 pay 1000 to an attacker who survives a lost round without planting and to a defender who survives a detonation, below the 1900 loss bonus floor, and every sidearm costs less than that gap

text: On a save round, a rifle you pick up off the ground is only worth something if you are alive when the round ends, so once you have it stop hunting and hide, because the gun you carry over is next round's buy.
when: the player picks up a primary during an eco or lost pistol round
why: a carried rifle is a full rifle's price saved, a dead body with it is nothing

text: Take the ultimate orb before the spike goes down when it sits on your path, because every orb vanishes the moment the plant finishes and the point is gone with it.
when: attack side, orb near the site being hit, plant about to happen
why: the existing orb note says grab orbs when a fight is over, this adds the deadline

text: On a save round, play for one kill and the orb on your side, because kills and orbs still charge your ultimate on a round you expect to lose and a charged ultimate is what makes your next buy round different.
when: eco round in the active phase, ultimate not yet charged
why: ultimate points come in equal from kills, deaths, orbs and the spike, so an eco is the cheapest round to charge on

text: When you start the retake late and the spike is already beeping fast, go straight for the half defuse, step off with your gun ready and finish it after, because a full defuse started that late is a coin flip against anyone still watching the spike.
when: defender arriving on site with the fast beeps already playing
why: the existing half defuse note covers the clutch, this covers the arrival timing that decides whether a full stick is even possible

text: After the plant, keep one piece of utility for the last seconds instead of throwing it at the first noise, because a molly on the spike as the defuse starts wins the round and the same molly on a wall earlier wins nothing.
when: attacker with a damage or slow ability still up after the plant
why: a defuse must be interrupted to lose time, so the utility is worth most once it starts

text: Never reload while you are watching the spike, swap to your sidearm or reload behind cover before you take the angle, because a half defuse that starts during your reload is one you cannot punish.
when: attacker holding the spike with a partly empty magazine
why: the defuse checkpoint banks in a few seconds, about the length of a rifle reload

text: When you hear the defuse start, break their line of sight to the spike with a smoke, a wall or your body before you fight, because any interruption throws away everything they had before the halfway mark and buys you the time your teammate needs.
when: the defuse audio plays while the attacker still has smoke or a wall
why: progress before the checkpoint is lost on any interruption, so the cheapest interruption is enough

text: After your first kill in a clutch, aim at the spot the next enemy will come from before you loot, reload or move, because the fight is lost most often in the two seconds right after the first kill.

source.topic: pre aim the trade in a clutch

when: the player takes a kill while alone against two or more
why: the existing clutch kill note says move off the spot, this covers the beat before the move where the trade comes

text: In a clutch with no information, hold a spot they must cross rather than search for them, because a searcher meets the enemy on the enemy's terms and the clock or the spike makes them come to you.
when: last alive, no read on any enemy, no spike pressure on the player
why: the existing clutch notes assume some information, this is the rule when there is none

text: End the default once you have a live read on at least two defenders, and if you still have no read when utility runs low, lurk and drag the round out rather than execute dry, because an execute without a read or utility is five separate duels.
when: attack default past the middle of the round with little contact
why: the existing call the end of the default note says someone must call it, this says what the call should wait for

text: Turn on the shooting error graph (Video, Stats, Shooting Error, graph) and use it in the Range and in deathmatch, not in ranked, because a tall blue bar on a shot means you fired while still moving and tells you the miss was your feet and not your aim.
when: First shots of a duel show at the bottom of the graph in orange, a blue reading on the opening shot counts as a moving shot.
why: The game itself grades each shot for movement error, so the player stops guessing whether they stopped before firing.

text: At close or mid range fire two or three bullets on first sight, step sideways and fire again only if every bullet missed, and the moment one connects stay on the same target and keep firing, a full spray up close and another short burst at mid range, because strafing away to reset after a hit hands them the time to shoot back.
when: In five lost duels count the ones where you kept strafing after landing a bullet, the target is zero.
why: The first burst decides most fights, and a hit means the crosshair is already on them.

text: When you hear them running at your angle hold your crosshair wider off the corner, and when it is quiet hold it tighter to the edge, because a running player swings wide and fast while a quiet player creeps out at the edge.
when: Before each hold say whether you heard them, heard means a body width or more off the corner, silent means at the edge.
why: The right crosshair offset depends on how the enemy will arrive, and the sound tells you that before they show.

text: Never open a new angle holding only the forward key, step into it sideways with a strafe or a short jiggle and keep the forward key for ground you have already cleared, because a player sliding straight forward into an angle is slow to stop and easy to track.
when: Watch one round of your own, every new angle opened with the forward key alone is a count against you.
why: Sideways movement is the fastest you have and lets you stop and fire the instant someone shows.

text: Watch the sound ring drawn around your own icon on the minimap while you move, and shift walk the moment a known or likely enemy position sits inside it, because that ring is the game showing you exactly who can hear your steps.
when: Before each run between areas check whether the nearest enemy spot is inside your ring, a run with a known enemy inside it is the mistake.
why: Running is heard through walls and the ring removes the guesswork about when to go quiet.

text: Do not reload by reflex after a kill, read the counter and when a rifle still holds ten or more bullets keep the gun up on the next angle, because the reload is loud and the next enemy arrives during it.
when: After a kill with ten or more rifle rounds left, no reload until you are behind cover with nobody close.
why: The seconds after a kill are when the trade comes, and an empty animation cannot shoot back.

text: Hold your machine gun scoped when you sit on an angle or spam a wall, because scoped it fires at its top rate from the first bullet while hip fire starts slower and has to spin up, and fire from the hip only when you are moving or swinging and need the first shot at once.
when: Every held angle or wall spam with the Odin is fired through the scope.
why: The game data gives the Odin a rate of fire increase while aiming down sights.

text: Before you take a duel name the advantage you hold, more players at the fight, a flash or scan already used, or an angle they do not expect, and when you cannot name one and the clock does not force you, do not swing, because a fight that comes down to raw aim alone was lost in the preparation.
when: For each death name which of the three you had, a death with none is the one to fix.
why: Numbers, utility and angle are the three things a player controls before the shot.

text: Before a long peek name the gun on the other side, and when it is a sniper do not take the dry long fight with a rifle, take a different angle or bring a flash, because the duel is decided by the weapons before either of you aims.

source.topic: respect the gun across the angle

when: No dry peek of a known sniper angle in the match, every look at it is behind utility or from a new spot.
why: A sniper wins a long sightline against a rifle most of the time, so the fix is the choice of angle.

text: Whatever agent you play set up one first fight each round that you are favoured to win, with a piece of utility, a position or a two player plan, rather than waiting for a duelist to open the round for you.
when: Per half count the rounds where your first fight had utility or a plan behind it, a first duel with neither is the miss.
why: A round's first fight decides its numbers, and a prepared fight is the one most often won.

text: When you die first more often than you kill first, stop taking the opening peek alone, because at the top level the median opener still dies first about as often as they kill first, and the ones who keep opening do it with a teammate close enough to shoot back.
when: Over ten matches compare your first deaths to your first kills, more first deaths means every first peek now waits for a teammate in range.
why: The opening duel is a team action, and the record shows who took it alone.

text: When you want a height position nobody expects, use Updraft while the barrier is still up, because the jump is loud and an updraft heard once the round starts tells them exactly where you are.
when: Any updraft meant to surprise is finished before the round timer starts, one heard after the barrier within earshot is a tell.
why: The barrier phase hides the sound, and the surprise is the whole value of the spot.

text: Do not click while the crosshair is still travelling, land it on the enemy, confirm it with your eyes and then shoot, and after a miss make one deliberate correction and click again instead of hammering the fire key, because spam clicks pull the gun into its spray before the crosshair arrives.
when: In a replay a burst of three or more clicks at one target without the crosshair landing on them is the miss to count.
why: Most missed opening shots at low rank are fired before the crosshair reached the target.

text: When Cypher's ultimate snapshots you, expect a second snapshot shortly after and be behind different cover by the time it lands, and when his camera dart hits you, get behind cover first and then pull it out, because each snapshot is a still picture of where you stood but the dart keeps taking new ones until you remove it.
when: Within three seconds of being snapshotted you are behind different cover.
why: Riot's 13.09 notes changed the reveal to a snapshot rather than live tracking.

text: When you are nearsighted step back to a teammate or behind the nearest cover at once, because while it lasts your minimap does not show enemies beyond the short range you can see, even ones your teammates spot, and the angle you were holding is now a guess.
when: A nearsighted hold that keeps its spot and dies is the miss, the fix is the step back.
why: Riot's 13.09 notes made nearsight hide the minimap beyond its own range.

text: Grade a lost one versus many on the decision and not the result, because even professionals win only about one in seven of these and the very best about one in four or five, so losing one is the normal outcome and the question is whether you kept the gun, took one fight at a time and played the clock.
when: Over your last twenty clutch situations three or four wins is already a top level rate.
why: Treating every lost clutch as a mistake teaches the wrong lesson and tilts the next round.

text: In a two versus one push only when both of you will see the enemy in the same moment, one wide and one tight from the same corner or a crossfire with the trade ready, because two players arriving one at a time are two one versus ones for the enemy.
when: Before the push ask whether you round the corner within a second of each other, if not, wait.
why: The number advantage only exists while both guns are on the fight at once.

text: In a late round where you are down numbers, make loud noise in one lane, run, break a door or trip a wire on purpose, then go quiet and move to another lane before you fight, because the enemies have to split their attention between two places you could be.
when: Your last loud sound and your next shot come from different lanes.
why: A team that knows where you are plays the retake as a unit, a team guessing plays it apart.

text: When you are down numbers on defence, position on the path you expect them to take, wait for a footstep, a reload or a utility sound on your line, and step out on that cue rather than on a guess, because a static hold waits to be found and a blind peek walks into two guns at once.

source.topic: numbers down peek on a cue

when: In a numbers down round every peek follows a sound you can name.
why: A sound cue tells you one enemy is busy or close, which is the only moment a lone defender wins a fight.

text: In a clutch, use the smokes still standing, your own or an enemy controller's, to cut the remaining enemies off from each other and take the one on your side of the smoke, because the cover that hides you from the others is what turns the fight into a one versus one.
when: When two remain and you hold a smoke it goes between them or on the wider approach before your first peek.
why: A clutch is won as a chain of isolated fights, and smoke is the fastest way to build one.

text: When you die, read the damage off your combat report and call the agent, the place and the number in one breath, and when you land a hit while alive call the hit and the gun, because a Classic body hit does not finish a player left at thirty and your teammate chooses the fight on that number.

source.numbers: valorant-api.com damage table: Classic body 26 to 30 m

when: Every hit you land and every death produces a call with a place and a damage number, and no complaint.
why: A count and a place without the damage leaves the next swinger guessing which enemy is hurt.

text: Say what your smoke, flash or recon is about to do and where, one or two words before you throw it, because a team that hears it moves with the ability and a team that only sees it moves after.

source.topic: name the ability before it leaves

when: Count the abilities you used on an execute without a word before them, the target is zero.
why: Utility is only worth its full value when a teammate acts on it in the same second.

text: When an enemy ability goes off with no effect, a wall into nothing, a flash nobody was near, a dog already sent, say the agent and the ability, because spent utility changes which pushes are safe for the next half minute.
when: Each enemy ability wasted in front of you gets a call, aim for none unspoken.
why: The team plans around utility it expects, and knowing it is gone opens a lane.

text: Word anything you say to a teammate about their play as the next action, swing with me, take this corner first, hold back next round, and never as a judgment of how they played, because one correction in voice costs more rounds than the mistake did.
when: Zero sentences in voice about what a teammate did wrong across the match.
why: Tilt spreads through the team faster than any plan, and an instruction changes the next round while a verdict only changes the mood.

text: Tie your minimap glances to sounds, each distant gunshot, voice line or ability you hear while you are not holding a fight yourself is the cue to look at the map, because the sound is the reminder and you never have to remember to look.
when: After every fight sound you hear, a glance at the map within a second, a round where you heard a fight and never looked is the miss.
why: The minimap shows where the fight is and where nobody has looked, and a habit tied to a cue survives the pressure of a round.

text: In solo queue do not try to run all five, ask one named teammate for one ability on one spot at one moment, flash this corner when I say, smoke that window before I go, because a specific request gets done and a general one gets nothing.
when: At least one request per half that names the teammate, the ability and the spot, a general can someone flash does not count.
why: Small plays with one or two teammates are what a ranked team can actually execute.

text: When two plans are called in the same round, follow the first clear one and start nothing else, because five players committing to an average plan beat a better plan that two of them half follow.
when: No player starts an execute or a lurk the first call did not include, disagreement waits for the next buy phase.
why: Two ideas at once is what makes an attack stall and a defence split.

text: On an execute say what you are doing, I am smoking here, I am flashing there, I am going first, instead of asking who will, because a statement lets everyone build the picture and a question stops the team to answer it.
when: During the execute you asked zero questions and named your own action before using it.
why: Hesitant calls produce two half plans instead of one full one.

text: The moment your push or lurk produces a result, a kill, a broken trip, an empty site or two defenders leaving, call it in the same second so a teammate uses the space it opened, because pressure nobody acts on is lost the moment the defence resets.

source.topic: call the result of your pressure

when: Each lurk event gets a call within a second or two, and when your utility made two defenders leave the spike moves toward that site within five seconds.
why: The space a lurk or a push creates lasts seconds, and the team only moves into it if told.

text: In a spread default have each group report what its lane showed and count out loud, two seen there, two seen here, so the lane that showed nobody is the site you hit, because the empty lane is the read and the count is how the team sees it together.
when: Before committing you can say how many enemies each lane showed and where the missing ones must be.
why: Painting the picture as a team turns five partial looks into one decision.

text: After you win the first fight of a push, hold the space you were fighting for, a jiggle for information or a molly on the approach and then back into the spot, and wait there for your team rather than wandering to another part of the map or falling all the way back, because a won duel followed by a wander gives the space straight back.
when: After an opening kill the killer's next action is to hold or deepen that space, not to cross the map.
why: The point of the opening kill is the ground it clears, not the kill.

text: After a lost pistol, if your team forces the second round and loses it, save the third round even if it hurts, because two failed forces in a row leave the whole team broke into the next buy and a force that keeps losing is a habit, not a plan.

source.topic: no second force after a lost pistol

when: Never two consecutive force buys after a lost pistol, the second round after a failed force is a save.
why: A small purchase on a round you then lose pushes the full buy back another round each time.

text: Do not buy a pistol and a shield on a round you have decided to save, because that small spend turns the next round into another eco and locks you into buy, eco, buy, eco, so aim for the rhythm of buy, eco, buy, buy, and keep any eco spend to cheap abilities that leave the next full buy intact.

source.topic: half buy makes the next eco

when: Count your pattern over a half, alternating buy and eco more than once means you half bought on an eco.
why: Back to back full buys are what win halves, and every half buy on an eco costs one of them.

text: On the save round after a lost pistol keep enough credits that what you carry plus the 2,400 loss bonus still buys a rifle, armour and your abilities in round three. With no kills in the pistol round that means a full or near full save, and anything you do buy, a light shield or a Ghost, comes only out of what your pistol round kills or plant earned.
when: Your round two spend is one category only and your credits after the round still allow a rifle, armour and abilities.
why: The credits after a lost pistol stretch to one upgrade, and the round after needs the rest.

text: Before you buy armour look at the shield number you carried over, and when it is still full or close to it keep it and put the credits into the gun and abilities, because shields you survived with stay with you and buying the same armour again replaces it rather than stacking on top.
when: Each buy phase you check the shield number before pressing armour, and never rebuy after a round where you took no damage.
why: Shields carry over between rounds and rebuying one you did not lose throws away a buy two rounds later.

text: On a full buy have your key abilities bought, the smokes, the flash or the info tool your plan needs, and at least light armour or the regen shield before you upgrade to heavy, because a smoke at a choke or a wall on a lane denies them the raw gunfight they want and the extra shield only matters once that fight is already fair.
when: Heavy armour appears on your buy only when every ability is already bought, and no buy round starts with zero shield.
why: Utility shapes the fight, armour only survives it a little longer.

text: When your team wins the pistol, everyone buys a gun and armour in round two, and nobody stays on a pistol to match a teammate who saves, because the round against a broke team is yours to lose and a short handed buy turns it, and the third round, into a coin flip.
when: Five guns with armour on your team in round two after a pistol win, zero saved pistols.
why: The anti eco is the one round where matching a saving teammate is wrong.

text: Hold the scoreboard in every buy phase and say what they can afford, a sniper, a force, shotguns, then name one angle you will not peek this round because of it, because the enemy buy decides which fights are good before anyone moves.

source.topic: read their buy before the barrier

when: Before the barrier drops you can say the enemy's likely buy and the one area you avoid for it.
why: A dry peek into a sniper or a corner push into shotguns is lost in the buy menu, not in the fight.

text: When most of the enemy hold less than a rifle and Light Armor cost together, about three thousand three hundred credits, they cannot full buy, so expect a shotgun, an SMG or a cheap rifle held in a close corner, and do not walk past a tight spot without an ability to check it first.

source.numbers: valorant-api.com damage table: rifle cost 2900, Light Armor 400

when: In the buy phase note the enemy average, around three thousand or lower means close corners are cleared with utility or avoided.
why: A team that cannot afford rifles buys the guns that win inside a doorway.

text: On a save round name before the barrier the one fight you can win with what you hold and the spot you will take it from, take it with a teammate close enough to trade, and stay alive everywhere else, because four deaths for one kill hands them the round and the guns, while a survivor keeps whatever gun and shield he carries into the next buy.
when: On an eco at least four of five teammates alive at the end or the spike planted with the team intact, and you fired at an enemy from a spot you chose.
why: A save round has two jobs, one favourable fight and five survivors, and hiding does neither.

text: On an eco put your two best guns together on one site with a trap, one on a wide off angle and one ready to swing off the first contact, and have the other site avoid every duel until the numbers change, because five pistols spread across the map lose every fight one at a time.
when: On an eco you can name which site holds the guns, and the players on the other site take no duel before the first kill lands elsewhere.
why: An eco wins by making one fight favourable, not by covering the map.

text: Before the team settles on a save, count the ready ultimates that replace a gun or win a fight on their own, because a player holding knives, a sniper ultimate or a lightning beam plays the round as a full buy, and a lockdown or a wave that tips an eco is often worth more there than kept for a buy round by habit.
when: In the buy phase of a save round you name every ready weapon ultimate before anyone presses buy.
why: A weapon ultimate is a free gun this round and nothing next round.

text: When you lost the pistol and then win a round, treat the very next round as the one the half depends on and set the target as two wins in a row, buy fully and commit your utility and any ready ultimate, because a loss there pays only the base loss amount with no streak bonus and forces an eco the round after.

source.topic: the round after the comeback win

when: After a win that followed losses your next buy is a full one and your ultimate is used in it if ready.
why: A win resets the loss bonus, so the next loss is the poorest paid round of the half.

text: When the kill feed has shown an Outlaw on their side buy heavy armour with your rifle, because one body shot from it kills through a light shield and not through a heavy one, and only consider light armour to bank credits when no sniper has appeared.
when: Outlaw seen means heavy armour on your next buy.
why: The Outlaw's body damage sits exactly between what light and heavy armour survive.

text: Do your buy in the first seconds of the buy phase and spend the rest of it walking to where you start the round and placing any setup utility, because a player still shopping when the barrier drops begins the round late and out of position.
when: Every round you are at the barrier with your buy done before the ten second mark.
why: A player still shopping when the barrier drops starts the round out of position.

text: When you review a death ask first what decision twenty seconds earlier put you in that spot, whether you needed to be there at all, before you judge how you played the fight, because a perfect retake does not matter if you should never have been in a retake.
when: For each death write one line naming the earlier decision, and fix that before the aim.
why: Most deaths are decided before the duel, and the aim is the last thing to blame.

text: When you notice you are thinking about the result, the rank, proving yourself, not messing up, replace it with one concrete job for the next round, crosshair at head height on this hold or a clear call on first contact, and judge the round by whether you did that job.
when: One named job per round said to yourself in the buy phase, a round where you did it counts as a good round.
why: A single easy task pulls the head off the last mistake, and a job can be done whether or not the round is won.

text: When you are down on the scoreboard do not go and take a fight to fix it, keep playing the round at the speed it asks for and let the fights come from your position, because the wide swing taken to feel better is the one that loses the round as well.
when: After a death that leaves you well behind on the board your next round has no solo wide swing in its first twenty seconds.
why: Nobody is counting your mistakes, and a forced duel after a bad half is the most predictable death in the match.

text: After a lost round, and again after a lost match, name one thing you could have done differently before you think about what any teammate or any enemy did, because the player who blames the lobby while making their own mistakes is the one who stays at the same rank.
when: One self correction named per lost round, before any word about a teammate, a smurf or luck.
why: Your own play is the only variable you control, and a review that starts elsewhere finds nothing to fix.

text: Judge whether a change in your play is working by your win rate over your last twenty to thirty matches and not by one match's rank rating, because the number you see is a smoothed version of a hidden rating that moves every game and a single match tells you nothing.

source.topic: judge the climb by win rate

when: Count wins and losses over the last twenty to thirty matches before deciding whether a habit change worked.
why: Riot has published how rank rating follows the hidden rating, and the only input that moves it meaningfully is winning.

text: Keep playing full rounds when the match looks lost and do not vote to surrender early, because the score margin still feeds your rank, a surrender counts every remaining round as lost, and a team behind after a bad first half still has a full half on the other side to come back in.

source.topic: every round of a lost match counts

when: When down by six or more the goal is the next round, no buy throwing and no save spam, and no surrender vote from you before the second half.
why: Riot's own matchmaking post says the margin of the result feeds the rank.

text: Keep a small pool of two to four agents you can play at full comfort, built around one role with one agent in a second role for when yours is taken, because a kit you have to think about costs you the attention the round needs.
when: Your last twenty ranked matches use at most four agents, and at least one is in a second role.
why: The agent's abilities have to be automatic before the reads and the calls can be.

text: Play each deathmatch with one named habit for the whole game, clearing each corner with your crosshair already on it, peeking one angle at a time, or holding with your crosshair at head height, and judge the session by whether you kept it on every life, not by the score.
when: Before the deathmatch you can say the constraint, and after it whether you kept it on every life.
why: A deathmatch played to win trains nothing, a deathmatch played for one habit changes it.

text: Warm up the same way before every session, a few minutes in the range and one deathmatch, finished inside about twenty minutes, because a different routine every day gives a different player every day and a long warm up eats the focus it was meant to build.
when: One deathmatch at most two before the first ranked queue, the same order each session, finished inside twenty minutes.
why: The warm up is for reaching the same focused state, not for improving.

text: Keep the crosshair at the height a head will actually be for the angle you are opening, lower for a far target and adjusted for stairs, boxes and raised ground, because a crosshair set for a far peek sits above a close head and a flat head height on a slope lands on a chest.
when: Before each peek name where the head will be for that angle's distance and elevation, and after a lost duel check whether the crosshair sat at that height.
why: Head height is not one line, it moves with distance and elevation.

text: After each kill or cleared corner move your crosshair deliberately to the next spot you have not cleared and stop it there at head height, never resting it on ground you already know is empty, because the flick you then need is a few degrees instead of ninety.

source.topic: crosshair to the next uncleared spot

when: At the moment an enemy appears your crosshair is within a head's width of their head sideways, count the times it was on a cleared spot instead.
why: A crosshair parked on cleared ground is the wide flick that loses the next fight.

text: Do not blame the agent picks for a loss at your rank, two duelists and no sentinel is playable, the only missing role that really hurts is smokes, so if nobody takes them take them yourself and otherwise play the match.

source.topic: a comp decides little at your rank

when: If the lobby has no controller at the end of agent select you lock one, and no comp complaint appears in your review of the match.
why: At Gold and below the duels and the trades decide rounds long before the comp does.

text: On the pistol round, when your first hit lands on the body of a player who bought no armour, fire again at once, because a second body hit kills them, but against any shield two body hits leave them alive, so keep the crosshair at head height and the body shot is the follow up, not the plan.

source.numbers: valorant-api.com damage table: Sheriff body 55 to 30 m

when: On pistol rounds your kills on unarmoured players come from two body hits, and against a light shield you took the fight from a held head level angle.
why: Most players skip armour on the pistol round, and the body hit is the easier one to land.

text: When a slow attack has won you several rounds keep playing it until the defence shows you an answer, a stack, early aggression or a new setup, and do not flip to a fast hit after one lost slow round you can explain by a lost duel, because changing what wins before they have adapted throws away the read and a change after every loss makes the half feel random.
when: After three rounds won at one tempo the next round keeps it unless the enemy has visibly changed their setup.
why: The enemy adapts to what beats them, not to what you abandoned.

text: Before you borrow a position or a play from a professional match, say the situation it was made for and the one it is not, because much of what you see there is a prepared answer to one opponent and a timing measured in seconds that does not transfer on its own.
when: For every borrowed setup you can state when it applies and when it does not, and you review whether it worked.
why: A play copied without its condition fails at the first contact that goes differently.

text: Measure consistency as the share of your games you played to your plan and not as never playing badly, because even a professional has bad games, and the work on fundamentals moves that share from six in ten toward seven and eight, never to ten.

source.topic: consistency is a share of games

when: Over your last twenty games count the ones played to your plan regardless of the scoreboard, and aim to raise it by one or two per twenty.
why: A player who expects every game to be good reads a normal bad one as a collapse.

text: Once a half take one swing or one timing you would normally not take, in a round where losing it does not break your economy, and after the match note whether it worked and why, because a player whose position and buy can be predicted every round is the easiest player on the map to prepare for.
when: One deliberate new play per session written down afterwards with worked or did not and the reason.
why: Limit testing on purpose is how a playbook grows, and the review turns the test into knowledge.

text: Shoot the enemy where they are drawn on your screen and never lead a moving target, because the server rewinds the world to the moment you fired, so what you saw is what gets checked.

source.topic: shoot where the model is drawn

when: Crosshair on the model, not in front of it, and a run of misses on moving targets is checked for leading first.
why: Riot's netcode article explains the rewind, and leading is a habit from other games that misses here.

text: When you die while still shooting and the kill feed shows only your death, treat it as a timing loss and not a hit registration bug, because the server took their lethal shot first and ignores the shots you fired after it, so take that fight next time from a position where you see them before they see you rather than re peeking the same angle harder.

source.topic: a trade on your screen that was not

when: A death that looked like a trade on your screen with only your name in the kill feed is followed by a change of position, never a re peek.
why: The fix for a lost timing is the position, and a re peek only repeats the timing.

text: Hold still on a common angle only when you have an off angle, a teammate who trades the swing, or utility that makes them peek into you, because the game gives the mover the first look and a holder with none of those is the one losing the coin flip.

source.topic: hold still only with a reason

when: Per half count the duels where you stood still for more than three seconds on a common angle with no utility and no teammate covering you.
why: Riot's own articles measure the peeker's head start, and only preparation wins it back.

text: When you land a body shot on someone who peeked you in the open keep firing at the same target, because a tagged player is slowed and cannot get back behind the corner at full speed, so your next bullets are your best chance at the kill and not a new duel.
when: After a hit marker on a peeker your next bullets go to the same target without re adjusting, and if they escaped behind cover after one hit you stopped too early.
why: The slow on hit is a game rule and the retreat is its worst option.

text: When you have to clear a corner you are standing close to, do not creep or lean around it with a shift walk, step off the wall first and clear it in one fast wide step with your crosshair already at head height on the far edge, because a slow edge shows your shoulder to the holder long before you see them. If you already know someone holds it, use utility or a quick jiggle for the information before you commit the swing.
when: Every corner you believe holds an enemy is cleared in one wide step, with no shift walk and no diagonal forward key.
why: The close corner peeker is seen first, and only speed takes that back.

text: When you peek, end your strafe at the spot you chose before the enemy's position enters your screen and shoot from a standstill, and when you clear a series of angles stop briefly at each one so the crosshair is set before the next opens, because a player who swings wide, sees the enemy and then tries to stop fires while sliding.
when: One full stop per angle, and you are never mid strafe at the moment a new angle opens.
why: The stop has to come before the sighting or the first bullet is a moving one.

text: Use a crouch tap only now and then as a change of pace, on a repeek or against a holder you have seen sitting at standing head height, tapping it as you clear the corner and standing straight back up, and never crouch before the peek starts, because a predictable crouch drops your head into a crosshair held low.
when: One crouch tap timed with the first shot of the peek, then up, and in deathmatch before ranked.
why: The holder pre aims a standing head, and the tap steals the first shot without costing your movement.

text: Do not stop your swing exactly where a holder's crosshair rests, swing wider than the natural stopping point or go so tight that your model never reaches it, and never give the same default swing twice on one angle, because most holders stand a default distance off the wall and aim where everyone stops.
when: Your stop point is past the edge of the cover, and across a half your peeks on one angle are not all the same width.
why: A holder wins by prediction, and a swing that ends somewhere else forces them to move the mouse.

text: When footsteps or a call tell you an enemy is coming to your corner, decide before they reach it whether you trust the hold or swing early, and settle the crosshair and commit to the shot in advance, because the half measure where you start peeking as they peek loses to either choice.

source.topic: decide hold or swing before they arrive

when: Never start a peek within the second the enemy's peek starts, and when a teammate calls a position you hold you say swing incoming and set the crosshair.
why: A hold with information is not a reaction test, it is a decision already made.

text: When your entry utility pops go within the next second, and when you are going to cancel, cancel early, because hesitating after the stun or flash lands and then going late into a site that has now stacked loses rounds either clear choice would have won.

source.topic: go on the pop or cancel early

when: Once your entry ability lands you are on site within two seconds or you have called off, and the time from a flash landing to your swing is under one second.
why: Utility buys a window of seconds, and a late entry arrives after it closes.

text: When your last hit through one choke was stalled by a single molly or blind, come at that site from two directions next time, with two players at the main choke, one holding pressure and one using utility, because one piece of utility stalls one choke completely and it takes twice the utility to stall both halves of a split.

source.topic: split when one piece stalled you

when: After a hit stalled by one ability the next hit on that site comes from two directions with at least two players at main, one holding and one blinding.
why: A split only works if both halves are real, and a lone player at main is not a split.

text: When the defence spends the one ability that stops your hit on a fake, a blind on the choke or a wall into nothing, hit that site within the next few seconds before it recharges, and when you hear their utility going off on the far side of the map, hit the site you are on before the rotation arrives.

source.topic: hit when their stopper is burned

when: From the enemy's far side utility or their burned stopper to your first player on site is under five seconds.
why: The window after a wasted stopper is the cheapest entry of the round.

text: When a teammate's flash, stun or missiles land on a group, be shooting into that group within two seconds rather than backing away or diving a different target, because the utility is only worth anything while someone swings on it.
when: When a teammate's damaging or blinding utility lands on enemies you are firing into them within two seconds.
why: A teammate's push is your window, and a flash nobody swings on is wasted.

text: Do one thing at a time in a duel, either finish the enemy and accept the utility piece coming at you, or step off the angle, break the utility and re peek, and never holster your gun for an ability while the enemy who ducked back can re swing you.
when: One target per peek, and your gun is never down for utility unless the enemy is confirmed gone or you are behind cover.
why: The swap is the moment you cannot shoot back, and the re swing is timed for it.

text: When the same dart, drone or dog lands on your spot two rounds running, shoot it the moment it appears and leave the spot before the swing comes, or step out of the spot before it lands and take the fight while they are still throwing it, because a position their recon clears every round is a position they have already pre aimed.

source.topic: break the repeated recon and move

when: After you break a recon you change position by at least one piece of cover, and a recon that lands on you a third time finds you gone.
why: Enemies reuse lineups, and a holder revealed in the same place twice is the easiest kill of the round.

text: When a teammate's recon or drone is about to reveal a site, hold your angle until it pings or the teammate calls clear, then peek off the information beside them, because a peek taken while the drone is still flying wastes both the utility and the fight.

source.topic: peek on the ping not the throw

when: Your feet stop when a teammate's recon goes out and your swing comes on its ping or its end, side by side with a teammate.
why: The reveal is the point, and the swing before it is a dry swing with extra noise.

text: When a teammate commits to a peek you would not have taken and you cannot stop them, swing with them and take the trade instead of leaving them to die alone, unless three or more enemies are on that angle, because two players making the same bad play together beat one dying for nothing.
when: When a teammate near you starts a peek you are shooting their angle within a couple of seconds of their first shot, and against three or more on the angle you fall back instead.
why: A trade turns a bad peek into an even fight, and a stack turns it into two deaths.

text: By round three know which enemy is the aggressive one and the two spots they have shown up from, say it to your team and expect that agent early and forward, because in ranked people repeat what wins and the pusher is the easiest read in the match.
when: After three rounds you can name the enemy who pushes and the spots they pushed from.
why: A pattern named out loud is one the whole team can set a crossfire for.

text: The round after you punish a repeated play, do not reset the same trap, expect that player to have moved, often to the other side, and set up for the move rather than the habit, because a player who got caught assumes you will be waiting there again.
when: The round after a punish you check the opposite side first and do not reset the same trap.
why: Good players adjust once, and the counter to the adjustment is the next free kill.

text: In solo queue pick and learn two or three agents whose kit still pays off when nobody plays around it, a flash you can swing on yourself, a smoke you can play off alone, a setup that holds a site by itself, because utility that only works with a coordinated teammate goes unused, and an agent like Astra or Yoru wants hours in a custom before ranked.

source.topic: solo queue agents create your own kills

when: If you solo queue below Immortal and your agent has fewer than two abilities you can shoot off yourself, change agent.
why: Solo queue rewards the player whose kit works without coordination.

text: Do not rotate off your site on one flash, one knife or one recon dart alone, wait for a second signal, the footsteps of more than one attacker, the hit's other utility landing with it, or the spike call, and leave the anchor behind when you go, because a single ability with nobody behind it is the cheapest fake there is.
when: Your team rotated only after a second signal, a second ability, a player seen or a plant sound, never after one ability alone.
why: A rotation needs two signals, and a single ability is one.

text: Once a route or a site hit has been stopped, change something before you run it again, the split, the path or the timing, because a defence that has seen the same push learns where to stand, and a hit that worked twice and then fails is one they now expect.

source.topic: do not hit the same site five deep twice

when: Over a half no entry route is used three attack rounds running once it has been stopped, and a five player hit on one site is repeated only while it keeps winning.
why: Repetition on attack trains the defence for free.

text: Judge each round by one question, did you kill, assist, survive or die where a teammate traded you, and work to shrink the rounds where the answer is none, because a typical professional fails all four in about three rounds of every ten and the very best still in about two, and the round with nothing is almost always an early death nobody traded.
when: After a match count the rounds with no kill, no assist, no survival and no trade, at twenty four rounds seven or fewer is a top level number.
why: The round with nothing is the one to review first, and it is almost always an untraded early death.

text: Do not judge a match by the kill column alone, professionals average about seven kills every ten rounds and the steady middle of them runs from six to eight, so sixteen or seventeen kills in a twenty four round match is an average game at the top, judge the match by the rounds you contributed to and by how you died.
when: Over twenty matches kills per round near seven in ten and a kill to death ratio near one are the professional norms.
why: The kill column measures the wrong thing and a player protecting it saves when the round is winnable.

text: Every defence round take one deliberate information action between about a minute ten and forty seconds on the clock, a jump peek, a dart, a drone or a rehearsed small push, because if the first sign of the hit is five attackers on your site your information failed earlier in the round and not your hold.
when: By forty seconds on the clock your team has gained one piece of fresh information, and each site loss is marked by whether a call about numbers or direction came before the first enemy touched site.
why: The defence cannot explore the way an attack can, so the information has to be planned.

text: Play most ranked defence rounds as one strong site and one weak site, the strong side with the players and the utility to deny the plant, the weak side stalling the choke with utility and playing for the retake, and name the lanes you give up, because thin holds everywhere hand the attack isolated duels and you end up holding nothing.
when: Before the round you can say which site is strong and which is weak, and no lane is held by one player with no teammate able to trade within a few seconds.
why: Five players cannot hold every lane, and a defence that chooses is a defence that trades.

text: Before you lurk say which job it is, arriving behind the defenders while your team is fighting them or taking space for a rotate, and once your team is on site move up and threaten that flank or rotation, because a lurk that has done nothing by the time the team is dead was too slow.

source.topic: a lurk has one of two jobs

when: You can name the job before you go, your lurk step past the first choke comes after your team's contact shows on the map, and your first shot comes before the team is dead.
why: A lurk that threatens nothing is playing four against five.

text: Before you tuck into a spot on site look at the minimap and ask which entry a teammate already holds, then hold the one nobody holds rather than the one you are nearest, because two players on one door and none on the other is a site with a hole in it.
when: Each defender on a site covers a different entry, and at any moment your crosshair covers an angle no teammate beside you covers.
why: A site is held by the angles covered, not by the bodies on it.

text: After your team gets the first kill your job changes to converting, stop looking for a second opening pick, regroup to trade range and play the number advantage out together, because a half lost while winning most opening duels is lost in the seconds after the pick.
when: After a first kill count the seconds before your next peek, a re peek within three seconds without a teammate set to trade is chasing, and rounds won after your team's opening kill should sit around seven in ten or better.
why: The round after the pick is where numbers advantages are thrown.

text: When you are the duelist left on a site, secure one line for a pick or an early call and then fall back and let the team rotate, and do not hold a one and done angle on an entrance with no teammate close enough to trade you, because a flash followed by a pinch kills you for free and the deeper angle buys the time instead.
when: After the first contact or pick you have left the forward line within a few seconds, and when the nearest teammate is more than one swing away your angle is the deep one.
why: A duelist's kit opens fights, it does not stall a site, and a lone forward angle is a free kill.

text: As the anchor of a site do not show yourself at barrier drop, take your first look after you hear or see the attackers commit, and do not take it from the spot where they saw or killed you last round, because an anchor whose position is known gets the opening utility and the pre aim, and one whose position is unknown gets the first shot.
when: Your first peek of the round comes after the attackers commit and never from the spot you fired from last round.
why: The anchor's value is being there alive when the hit comes, and a known spot is cleared first.

text: On defence, push out of your site only with a piece of information from this round, a camera, a trip, a sound or utility you just used, and do not repeat the same push the next round, because confidence is not information and a push that worked becomes the spot they pre aim or trap next time.
when: Before stepping past the site edge you can name the information from this round and the round in which the enemy was last seen there, and across a half you pushed the same angle at most twice and never in consecutive rounds.
why: Confidence is not information, and a repeated push is a known timing.

text: Do not take an aggressive defensive push across open ground without a smoke covering the longest sightline you will cross, because with no smoke the push is a dry run into a rifle.
when: Before an early push on defence you name the smoke that cuts the longest sightline, and when nobody has one you hold instead.
why: The long line is where the push dies before it learns anything.

text: When you are not the entry be the second contact, let the entry draw the attention and swing on their first shot one beat later from a step behind, with the minimap checked and the first contact pre aimed, because the second gun gets the kill with far less risk than the first.
