source.topic: play the first fight as second contact

when: Count the fights where you swung within two seconds of your entry's first contact against the fights where you swung alone.
why: The defender turns to the entry, and the trade a second later is the fight the second player wins.

text: Playing only as the support, most ability casts, most assists and plants and almost no first contacts, leaves the round in the enemy's hands, so add some impact of your own, take a duel your own utility set up, entry when the comp needs it and hold your own in a clutch, because playing too safe is also a mistake.
when: If your assists plus plants per match exceed your kills and you rarely take first contact, take one planned fight of your own per half.
why: The record shows the pure support profile gains the least, and a player who never dictates a round only reacts to it.

text: Take free damage when it costs you nothing, spam a known position through penetrable cover and shoot the utility you can see, but only when the shots do not give away a spot you still need, because chip damage and pressure add up to won rounds and damage a teammate turns into a kill is your contribution to it.
when: Count the rounds where you dealt zero damage while alive for more than twenty seconds.
why: Fifty damage on an enemy a teammate then kills is an assist and a contributed round.

text: Do not hoard Displacement for a perfect moment, use it on the first fight that needs it, because it resets every two kills and a pull still in hand when the second kill lands has wasted the reset.

source.numbers: Riot's 13.09 notes: Displacement resets every two kills

when: In a round where you got two kills you cast Displacement at least twice.
why: Riot's 13.09 notes give Displacement a reset on kills.

text: Before you smoke a choke on defence say what the smoke buys your team, and when the answer is only comfort keep the line of sight, because a reflex smoke on your own main removes your view of the lane and hands the attack a free orb or a quiet execute timing.
when: Each defensive smoke has a stated purpose, you wait for a second of sound before a one way on main, and against a suspected SMG rush the long lines stay open.
why: A smoke is a trade of vision, and a trade with no plan behind it favours the side that is moving.

text: Jump peek for two things only, to spot for a call or to pull an Operator's shot from behind cover, and never to take a fight, because you cannot shoot accurately in the air and the landing is loud, and once the sniper has fired, the swing comes during the bolt, yours or a teammate's.

source.topic: jump peek only for a sniper

when: No jump peek in the match unless an Operator is holding the angle.
why: The jump buys one thing, a spent sniper shot, and costs sound and position everywhere else.

text: When you enter a site that opens to two sides have one side smoked, by your own ability or by asking your controller, and look at the other, and on the way in face only the angle no teammate is already holding, because a duelist who walks in exposed to both sides dies on a clean entry.

source.topic: smoke one side, face the other

when: On entry you are exposed to one unheld angle at a time, two open angles means one smoke before the step in, and your crosshair is on an angle no teammate faces.
why: Two open angles at once is the most common way an entry dies.

text: When you dash, satchel, sprint or propel onto a site, land beside cover or inside a smoke you can fight from, not out in the open, because an entry that lands exposed is cut off from the team and becomes one against several.
when: Every entry ends with a piece of cover within one step of where you land, and never beyond the first cover on the site.
why: The entry's job is a foothold the team can reach, not distance.

text: On an execute everyone crosses the choke while the entry smokes are still up and the flash is still active, nobody goes before the flasher's call and nobody stays behind after it, because an entry already on site with the rest of the team still behind the choke has failed before the first fight.

source.topic: through the choke while the smokes are up

when: Count the players past the choke when the smokes fade, fewer than four means the walk or the buy was too slow.
why: Utility buys a window of seconds for five players, not for one.

text: Around a fading smoke, swing either while it is still fully up or clearly after it has gone, never on the moment it clears, and swing wide enough that you end a full body width past its edge, because a smoke that has been up a while has an enemy crosshair waiting at its fading edge.

source.topic: swing a smoke early or clearly late

when: No smoke push more than a few seconds after it was placed, and your swing ends a full body width past the smoke's edge.
why: The fading edge is the most pre aimed pixel on the map.

text: On a fake the spike travels with the players making the real hit and not with the ones making noise, and a fake only counts if it moves the spike or takes ground you can hold, because a perfect distraction with the spike on the wrong side of the map still needs someone to walk back for it.

source.topic: the spike travels with the real hit

when: Before the fake starts the spike carrier is in the quiet group, and the fakers take ground they hold for at least ten seconds.
why: The plant is the point, and the fake is only worth the rotation it buys.

text: On Sunset defence close the door between Market and mid at the start of the round when nobody on your team is playing mid, and leave it open only while a named teammate is holding a mid line, because a duelist walks through an open door for a free timing behind a team that has already left.

source.topic: close the mid door when you rotate

when: The door closes as the first defender leaves the site to rotate, and stays open only while someone holds mid.
why: The door is a free piece of flank watch that costs one press.

text: When the defence holds early stall utility on the site you want, a stun, a grenade, a slow at the choke or a Viper orb, do not run into the entrance in the first seconds, wait outside until it is thrown or the orb drops and go in behind it, because a wall or a push that walks into the slow is spent before anyone uses it.
when: Against a stall heavy defence no attacker crosses the entrance in the first fifteen seconds unless the stall has already been used, and a slow seen on the ground is waited out before the wall goes down.
why: Stall utility is strongest against a team arriving on schedule.

text: Against a held sniper swing together with a teammate in the same moment or behind a flash, or fill every lane it could watch with smokes at once, and if one player draws the shot the next swings at once while the bolt cycles, never seconds later, because a sniper holding one line beats a slow sequence of single targets and loses to two at once.

source.topic: never peek a sniper one at a time

when: Against a held Operator both players show in the same swing or the swing waits for a flash, and every lane it could watch is smoked before anyone steps into it.
why: The sniper's power is one shot on one lane, and two targets or no lanes removes it.

text: Against a team with a flash to come out on do not hard hold the drop or the choke, stand off the angle, let the flash go off and let them come out wide, then peek off that contact into players who are already out, because the hard holder eats the flash and the player a step back gets the swing.
when: Against a flash agent your first exposure to the choke comes after you have heard or seen their flash, and you are behind cover when you hear them clearing toward you.
why: A flash agent's first play is the choke, and the choke holder is who it is for.

text: On Haven account for mid and front B every round, on attack get a camera, a dart or a body on front B before the site call, and on defence do not give it up without a fight, because whoever holds it sees and controls the rotations between A and C and a defence allowed to walk into mid for free flanks or retakes through it.
when: On Haven attack with a full buy one player has front B information before the site call, and before the execute one piece of information has touched mid.
why: Front B is the hinge of a three site map.

text: On defence contest early space only as a pair with one piece of utility already down, an initiator's knife or recon with a controller's smoke, and take the fight only once that setup is in, because a solo early peek with nothing behind it is a dry duel the attackers were waiting for.
when: Early contact is taken with one teammate in support and one piece of utility down, a solo early peek with no utility counts against you.
why: Early contact taxes the attack's utility only when the defender survives it.

text: Time a defensive flank to land when the attackers make loud contact at the front, a swing or a turret firing, and leave for it once you hear the attackers commit to the far side, because every attacker is looking forward at that moment and a flank that arrives ten seconds late meets a team that has turned around.
when: The flank is announced and triggered on the front fight's first shot, within two seconds of the commit sound.
why: A flank is a timing, not a route.

text: Note which site the enemy's stun, tether or big blind played on the last round, and which site took their early utility, then hit the other one, because the stall utility they spent on one side is utility they will not have for the retake on the other.

source.topic: hit where the stall was not

when: After each round you can name which site had the enemy initiator and the stall agent, and the next hit goes where they were not.
why: Even a lost round tells you where the defence keeps its stopping pieces.

text: When three or more teammates rotate to a site on a call, count who is still on the other one, and when the answer is nobody you stay, because a fake only works against a team that left a site completely empty and a trap firing on the far side is the cheapest fake there is.
when: At least one player stays on the far site until the plant or clear information arrives.
why: Over rotation gives away a site without a shot fired.

text: After two lurks that found kills go with the team next round, and never run two lurkers at once, because the defence now expects you on the flank, the timing is gone, and two players off on their own leave three who cannot take enough of the map.

source.topic: never three lurks in a row

when: Never three lurks in a row, and at most one player lurks at a time.
why: A lurk is paid for by surprise, and surprise does not survive repetition.

text: When you are the only duelist, your job on most rounds is to open the site with the team, so do not lurk on the far side while the team walks into the choke without you, and when the team wants a lurker let it be an agent whose kit still helps from across the map, a global smoker or a sentinel.
when: As the solo duelist you lurk in zero rounds, and a lurker on your team is a controller or a sentinel.
why: The team without its only entry has nobody to open the site, while a smoker or sentinel lurking still places utility for the hit.

text: When you break a defender's information piece on one side, a trip, a camera or a turret, expect them to send one or two players to watch that area, wait a few seconds for the reaction, then go quiet and hit the other site, because the reaction is what the broken piece bought.

source.topic: break the piece, then go quiet

when: After breaking the piece your team moves on the other route within about five seconds, with no further noise.
why: The defence answers what it hears, and the answer is the gap.

text: When the attackers leave mid empty round after round, take it with two or three players together before they commit and use that timing to arrive behind their hit, because a defence with no space outside the sites waits to be told where the round is.

source.topic: take the mid they give away

when: After two rounds with no attacker seen in mid, the next defence round has three players through it before the attack commits, and at a minute fifteen on the clock you can name one area outside the sites a defender holds.
why: Free space is information, and information on defence is early rotation.

text: Flank through the other main on defence only when the sound and the utility from the attackers' main tell you four or more of them are there and no sentinel trap watches your route, because the one attacker left behind on that route is the one the flanker never sees.

source.topic: flank only on a confirmed count

when: Before the flank you can say how many enemies were spotted elsewhere this round.
why: A flank is a bet on where the enemy is not, and the bet needs a count.

text: Set a five player post plant as two on site with a stall piece for the first retake, two outside with a lineup, an ultimate or a spam angle onto the spike, and one on the flank, because the retake then has to beat three layers instead of one and the defuse stays contested after the site pair dies.
when: After the plant you can point to who is on site, who is outside with something that reaches the spike, and who is on the flank.
why: Five players on the site die to one piece of retake utility.

text: Know two plants on every site and what each costs, the default that is safer to plant and harder to hold, and the open one that is harder to plant and easier to hold, and choose by which half of the round you are weaker in, because a spot picked only because it is the usual one is not a chosen plant.
when: For each site you attack you can say where the default and the open plant are and which of your post plant positions see each.
why: The spike is seen from the same angles whether you plant it or they defuse it.

text: Plant in the open spot only when the site is actually yours, every entrance a defender could use to see the spike is smoked, walled or watched by a teammate for the four seconds, and in solo queue ask one teammate by name to hold a lane first, because without that control the same spot is a death with the spike dropped in the open.

source.topic: the open plant needs the site

when: Before an open plant every entrance onto the spike is covered and a named teammate has confirmed the lane, otherwise you plant the default.
why: An open plant is a choice to make the defuse hard, and it only works with the lanes held.

text: Before the plant take the space around the site that your post plant will need, and when the spike goes down have at most two players on the site itself with the rest already on the retake routes, because a team standing behind the entry line at the plant has to fight into the back of its own site.
when: At the moment the spike is planted at least two of your team are inside or beyond the site rather than in the entry choke, and at most two stand on the site.
why: Map control is the goal and the plant is what it buys.

text: While the spike goes down, the players not planting each face a different uncleared entrance instead of watching the planter, and nobody reloads, swaps weapons or pulls a knife until it is planted, because the planter cannot shoot and the covered plant is what buys the time.
when: During the plant each duelist faces a different entrance, and no weapon swap, reload or knife until the spike is down while any side is uncleared.
why: The planter has no gun out, and the covered plant is what makes the open plant possible at all.

text: Before the retake starts say what you still hold for the spike, I have the molly, I have the wall, nothing on the spike so we peek, so the teammate on site stays hidden when the spike is tapped instead of peeking into the retake.

source.topic: say what you hold for the spike

when: After the plant you announced each unused ability, and before the enemy reaches the spike your teammate heard whether anything covers the tap.
why: A post plant is played differently with a tap in hand and without one.

text: Reach the plant with at least one piece that can reach the spike from off site, a molly, a grenade or an ultimate, and spend only what the hit needs on the way in, because the defenders' retake is stopped by the utility still in hand when they go for the defuse.

source.topic: one closing piece at the plant

when: At the plant your team still holds at least one molly, grenade or ultimate that can reach the spike from off site, and you have at least two abilities left for the retake.
why: The last seconds are won by the ability still in hand.

text: Read the spike and not the clock to know whether a defuse is still possible, the beeping speeds up at about twenty seconds left and again at about ten, and once the extra ring appears around the spike at about seven seconds left a full defuse can no longer finish, so leave instead of tapping unless the spike was already defused past its halfway mark, which needs only three and a half more seconds.

source.topic: the spike tells you the time
source.numbers: game-rules.json: spike beeps at 20 and 10 s, defuse 7 s with its half at 3.5 s

when: When the dark shards appear under the spike you leave rather than defuse, and a full defuse is started before the second speed up.
why: The spike's own signals are the only timer you can hear while you fight.

text: Retake from two lanes with the widest angle between them, never two that run side by side, because one attacker can crossfire two adjacent lanes and cannot cover two that are far apart, and time the second lane to arrive while the first contact is still going.
when: Count the retake lanes you used, two adjacent ones count as one, and the second retaker arrives from a different angle within two seconds of the first contact.
why: Two lanes side by side are one lane to the player holding them.

text: On a retake land utility on the plant spot and the common anchor spots before the first body enters, damage onto the planter, a stun onto the planter's side, a smoke on one crossfire angle and a flash on the other, and keep one piece to cover the defuse, because peeking into the post plant crossfire is the fight it was built to win.
when: Before the first retaker crosses the entrance at least one piece has landed on a known post plant spot, and a planter spotted is met with utility and not a peek.
why: The standard post plant crossfire is broken by utility or not at all.

text: Be at your retake position with a route into the site when the spike goes down and not still rotating, then take the site's exits and bring the flank in behind before anyone floods, and if the plant lands while you are caught in the open wait out their aggressive push and then play the full retake, because some teams play the seconds around the plant to punish an early flood.
when: At the plant sound you are in a retake position with cover, the team holds two of the three ways out before anyone enters, and no death comes within five seconds of the plant from running in.
why: A retake is attacking on a timer, and the timer starts before the plant.

text: On a retake your smokes are the most valuable piece because they cut several angles at once, so hold them until two teammates are set to swing behind them, value your life over the first fight, and stay linked to the group, because a dead controller means a dry retake.
when: The retake blind leaves your hand only when two teammates swing with it, and you are still alive when your third teammate reaches the site.
why: The retake's isolation of angles lives in the controller's kit.

text: When the hit comes count the teammates within reach of the site with utility ready, three or more means contest the plant, alone means delay and stay alive for the retake, and when your team has lost most of the map group on one site rather than spreading, because the site is the one place the attack has to end up.
when: Count teammates within reach when the hit comes, and when fewer than the attack's map control group on one site with utility saved.
why: The decision to hold or retake is a count, not a feeling.

text: Spend your ultimate within a few rounds of it charging, on a round you can still win or the one that decides a buy, because it is earned back and an ultimate held for a perfect round that never comes was rounds of value thrown away. Hold it longer only for a round you have already named.
when: No ultimate held for more than two rounds after it charges, and at the half the ultimates you used are within one of the ultimates you earned.
why: Ultimates are earned back, and the most successful players at the top cast them often.

text: Before each round check the enemy ultimates that are one or two points away and not only the ones ready, and glance at the enemy portraits along the top of the screen mid round, a portrait marked as ready means that ultimate can come out now, because the ultimate that arrives from a kill or an orb is the one that changes the round.
when: In the buy phase you can name every enemy ultimate within two points, and after a kill feed line you check the portraits once.
why: An ultimate you did not know about is the one you walk into.

text: When your team has two or more attacking ultimates up, agree the round in the buy phase, the site and the order, and use them together on one hit rather than one per round or one on a lurk, because defenders caught inside a combination cannot answer it.
when: Two or more ultimates up means a plan said aloud before the barrier drops and all of them used in the same hit.
why: Ultimates stacked are worth more than ultimates in sequence.

text: When you are one orb from your ultimate ask a teammate to hold the one angle that sees the orb, take it and leave together, and when an orb sits where you cannot take it safely hold its approach or contest it rather than ignoring it, because an orb you neither take nor deny charges an ultimate for the other side.
when: Every orb run has one teammate on its angle, and for each orb you can say whether your team farmed it or denied it.
why: Orbs are the cheapest ultimate points on the map, for both teams.

text: On defence put the Pit down early to lock a whole sector, and on attack hold it until your team owns the site and the spike is in, then use it, because getting it down there is the hard part and refusing it because it feels awkward loses rounds already won.
when: On attack the Pit is never thrown before the site is taken, and with the spike down and the Pit ready it goes down.
why: The ultimate's value is a space the enemy cannot enter, and after the plant they must.

text: With Blade Storm out keep moving and clear corners as a jump, because the knives are accurate in the air and a holder aiming at head height has to re aim while you keep full accuracy.
when: Your first knife peek of a corner is a jump, and you never stand still while the ultimate is out.
why: The ultimate removes the one rule that makes jumping bad.

text: Send Reckoning down the lane the flood or the re entry has to use and stop it there so it stands as a wall across that path, nearsighting and slowing whoever walks through, and on a retake end it across the attackers' way back in while you clear the site, because an ultimate that rolls past everyone and covers no path is wasted.

source.topic: the harbor ultimate covers a lane

when: Before casting you can name the lane the final pulse covers, and on a retake it lands on the spike spot within two seconds of the plant sound.
why: The ultimate's last wave is a wall, and the planter cannot move while it finishes.

text: Against a Killjoy, name early who breaks the Lockdown, shooting the device during its windup, a Brimstone ultimate or Tejo missiles onto it, and when nobody can reach it, call the team off the site and play the retake, because conceding a site to a Lockdown you could have broken is a round given away and stacking a site under one is a round lost twice.
when: Against a Killjoy your team has named who breaks the Lockdown before round one, and with no answer the team is off the site before it finishes.
why: The ultimate wins only against a team that stays in it.

text: Make Hunter's Fury a called round on attack, dart the site as the team moves and fire on the scanned players within seconds, and when you earn it in a numbers advantage with a tag on an enemy press it at once and back up as you fire, because an ultimate aimed at a habit or a reveal lands and one saved for a reaction never does.
when: Each attack ultimate fires on players a dart or a teammate revealed within five seconds of the reveal, and you are moving backwards during the shots.
why: The ultimate is three shots at where someone is, not at where they might be.

text: Pair the reveal with the flash: when your knife, dart or drone shows where a defender is, the flash on that exact spot, yours or the one you asked a teammate for, should land a second or two later so the team takes the spot before the defender moves, because information nobody acts on in the same breath is wasted.

source.topic: recon then flash within three seconds

when: Your flash follows your recon by no more than three seconds and lands on the spot it revealed, and the close piece is out before the deep one.
why: The reveal expires and the defender moves the moment it lands.

text: Do not sit in a drone or a camera while your teammates swing in, send the information piece before they go and be beside them with the gun in hand for the trade, and when a teammate is in a drone near you hold their angle without being asked, because a player piloting is blind and dead to any swing.

source.topic: out of the drone before the swing

when: When a teammate starts to swing your drone or dart is already out and you are within trading distance, and a teammate in a drone within ten metres has your crosshair on their angle.
why: The initiator's kills come from trades after the utility, not from the utility.

text: In Gold and below use your initiator utility for your own fight or for one teammate you are talking to, and swing on it yourself within a second or two, because a flash thrown for a teammate who has not asked for it goes unused and a round where you cast everything and never fired was a round you watched.

source.topic: utility for your own fight at low rank

when: Below Platinum every flash or scan you throw is followed by you or your duo swinging on it, and no round ends with utility used and no shot fired.
why: Coordinated set plays become reliable only around high Platinum, and until then the kit has to make your fights.

text: As the smoker do not take the first fight of the round before your smokes are placed, then put the gun up and play, because at the top level controllers are the first to die in well under one round in ten, and a first death before the smokes leaves the hit naked.

source.topic: the smoker lives until the smokes are down

when: Zero first deaths before your smokes are placed, your first death share stays under a tenth of rounds, and you still take a fight once the smokes are down.
why: The execute depends on the smokes more than on the controller's gun, and a controller playing scared after they are down loses rounds too.

text: Before you smoke on defence ask whether this is the smoke the attackers would throw for themselves, and if it is do not throw it, put the smoke on their side of the choke flush to its walls so they leave it into open ground with metres still to cross, because a smoke on the site's lip gives the pushers cover to play from.

source.topic: a defensive smoke is not an attacker's smoke

when: Your defensive smoke's edges touch the choke walls on the attackers' side, and the first attacker through it is visible to at least two defenders.
why: The side of the choke the smoke sits on decides who it helps.

text: Do not spend every smoke on early map control, keep enough in hand or on recharge for the execute and one for after the plant if your agent can, and do not call a slow default when the smokes are already on cooldown, because a smoke should serve the next step of the round, not only the first one.

source.topic: one smoke stays until the call

when: Before the barrier drops you can say which smoke goes to which phase, one is still in hand when the site is called, and no default is called with the smokes on cooldown.
why: A smoke should help the next step, not only the first one.

text: Bounce your flash off the ground or a low wall so it pops above or behind the enemy instead of throwing it flat across the opening, and throw it high over the roof line so they must lift their crosshair off your head to shoot it, because a flash they can watch for its whole flight is a flash they turn away from.
when: If the enemy can see the flash for more than a moment it was thrown flat, and the visible travel through a smoke is under half a second.
why: The flash they can see coming is the flash they dodge.

text: Name the enemy flash agents before the first round and decide before each peek that a flash may come, against a slow one hold slightly turned so one movement dodges it and you snap back, against a pop flash pre position where it cannot reach you and take the fight from there, because a player surprised by a flash turns late and a player expecting it turns first.
when: Before round one you can say the enemy flash agents, and each round you died fully flashed had either a turn or a position that should have beaten it.
why: Flash dodging is decided before the throw.

text: When enemy utility appears on your angle, an eye, a prowler, a dart or a camera, shoot it in the first second and snap the crosshair back to head height where they will come out, and shoot their early information pieces even when you will not fight for the area, because running from utility hands them the angle and a dead drone slows their whole default.

source.topic: shoot the utility and snap back

when: Utility is shot within the first second it is visible and the crosshair is back on the entry before they come through, and no dart or drone crosses your lane in the first fifteen seconds unshot.
why: The reveal is the expensive part of their round, and it costs you three bullets.

text: When enemy utility lands on the space you hold answer it with a piece that cancels it, a blind onto the flashers or a molly onto the push, and when more is coming than you can answer back off and keep your kit instead of taking the fight flashed, because the mid round is a utility count and the side one piece ahead decides the next fight.

source.topic: answer utility or leave with your kit

when: When you hold a spot you still have one ability unspent as the first enemy utility lands, and before you throw you can say whether you are holding or leaving.
why: Counter utility spent on space you will not hold is spent for nothing.

text: Place your trip, alarm or camera to watch the lane nobody on your team is standing in, so one angle is held by the utility and one by your crosshair, and on attack put the trip on the route behind the team within ten seconds of taking new ground, because a trap on the door everyone watches tells you nothing you did not know.

source.topic: trip the lane nobody stands in

when: At round start one lane your team is not standing in has a sentinel piece on its entry, and on attack a trip covers the route behind the team before the hit starts.
why: The sentinel's value is the lane it frees a body from.

text: Place your Rendezvous anchor before any fight and where you reach it faster than a dash or a slide reaches you from the angle you hold, take the one or two shots the spot gives and then teleport out instead of staying for another duel, because a Chamber whose anchor is slower than the push is another agent with a worse kit.

source.topic: the anchor must beat the dash

when: The anchor is down before every peek, and after the first kill at most one more shot before you press the teleport.
why: The teleport is the whole agent, and a late teleport is none.

text: Use your trap to take space and not only to watch your back: some rounds put it ahead into a corner or across a path the defence must cross, so breaking it forces them to show themselves into an angle you are holding, and keep your flank covered some other way when you do.
when: At least one trip per half goes in front of your line into a space you intend to take, and on attack the trip sits on a defender path and not in your spawn.
why: A trip in front of your line is information you can afford to spend.

text: Lock Viper as the second controller rather than the only one on most maps, and keep her setups simple, a wall, an orb and a held Snake Bite for the retake, because her wall and orb cover one site and a team with no other smoker is left short everywhere else.
when: At agent select Viper goes in after a controller is picked, and your defence setup is a wall plus an orb plus mollies kept for the retake.
why: Her wall and orb are a site, not a map.

text: Play Yoru simply while you learn him, the teleport to reposition or to leave a lost angle and then fight within a few seconds, and each Blindside popped for your own peek or for a teammate you called, because the kit is playable long before it is mastered and perfect lineups come later.
when: Every teleport is followed by a fight within three seconds, and for your first twenty games the teleport is an exit from a lost angle and the flash pops for your own peek.
why: The kit is playable long before it is mastered, and the simple version is the one that wins ranked rounds.

text: Place the turret so it opens fire on the attacker first and hold your crosshair where a player stands to shoot it, with the alarm on the floor at the entry and the swarm just behind, because an attacker who turns to the turret has turned away from you and an alarm that fires is the signal to detonate and call.
when: The turret covers the entrance you watch, your crosshair sits where someone stands to shoot it, and the swarm detonates the moment the alarm goes off.
why: The utility starts the fight and the gun finishes it.

text: Learn two or three basic recon or molly lineups per map for your main agent and otherwise throw by feel in the moment, a freehand dart or molly toward the main entrance still does its job, because a library of lineups costs practice time that fights and decisions need more at your rank.
when: You know at most two or three set lineups per map and a dart goes out before first contact every attack round, lineup or not.
why: One simple lineup wins more rounds than a dozen fancy ones.

text: Keep the drone for the moment the team commits onto the site, to clear the close corner the entry would otherwise check blind, or for a named threat you cannot approach, and do not spend it on space you already control, because a drone is slow, roots you while you fly it and tells the defence where you are looking.

source.topic: save the drone for the commit

when: The drone is still in hand when the team crosses into the site, and before any drone you can name the space you do not control that it checks.
why: The drone's value is the corner you have not cleared at the moment you need it.

text: Against a rush throw the slow onto the entrance they use the moment you hear them commit, before the first player is through, and stall with the wall rather than peeking, because the slow is your strongest tool against a rush, more than the heal, and once the hit is called your job is to buy time for the rotation, not to take the first fight.

source.topic: the slow is the anti rush

when: The slow or wall is used before a minute twenty on the clock in most rounds, and after the hit is called the Sage takes no first peeks.
why: A slowed rush dies to any crossfire, and the heal cannot stop one.

text: When Hush throws her flash or her pull, do not peek or turn towards it because the first arc looked like it was going past, she can redirect either one towards her crosshair while it flies, so turn away from the flash, stay behind cover, and take your peek after it has popped.

source.topic: wait for the pop against hush

when: Against a Hush you re peek on the pop and never on the throw.
why: Riot's 13.09 notes give her projectiles a redirect in the air.

text: When a Clove comes back with Not Dead Yet, stay on the angle you were holding and make them come to you, because the returned Clove must get a kill or a damaging assist or die, and the kill now pays you an ultimate point and a signature refresh while a swing out to chase them gives them the damage they need.

source.topic: a returned clove dies from your angle

when: When a Clove revives you stay on your angle for the seconds they have and let them come.
why: Riot's 13.09 notes reward the kill on a returned Clove, and the return has a short timer.

text: When an enemy ultimate or the first piece of a set trap lands on you use your movement ability at once to break the line or reach cover instead of trying to win the fight inside it, because a mobility duelist who dies with the escape unused gave the enemy the fight they built.
when: An enemy ultimate or stun on you is followed by the movement ability before you fire a shot.
why: A mobility duelist's kit is for leaving the fight the enemy chose.

text: Before you enter through a door a sentinel has set up, break every known trap on it with utility or bullets and never walk into one, send a drone, a dog or a clone first when you have one, and when a teammate is caught shoot the trap at once, because sentinel utility at a main is a reason to clear it and not a reason to stop taking space.

source.topic: break the trips on your door

when: A trip or camera spotted at a main gets a plan to break it within five seconds, none are walked into, and a caught teammate is freed inside two seconds.
why: A trip costs one ability to remove and one player to ignore.

text: Against a Neon take first contact from a distance her slide does not reach, and pre aim her entry as soon as you hear her sprint rather than after she appears, because her speed wins the position and loses to a crosshair already waiting at range.
when: Against a Neon rush nobody holds a close contact angle, and your crosshair is on her entry point on the first jump sound.
why: Speed wins the position and loses to a prepared crosshair at range.

text: On defence hold inside or right beside your own smoke early in the half, sometimes push into it and sometimes swing out of it as it fades, because attackers who learn they cannot run through a smoke at full speed slow down to clear every one, and later in the half a smoke with nobody behind it holds a lane while you rotate.
when: In the first three defensive rounds you held inside or at the edge of one of your own smokes at least once, and later you note whether an unmanned smoke slowed them.
why: A smoke only stalls a team that respects it, and respect is taught in the first rounds.

text: Against a Killjoy, when you are close to her setup, listen for the distinct sound her turret and alarmbot make when they switch off because she walked out of range, because that cue tells you she has left the site and what remains there is utility with nobody behind it.
when: When you hear the cue, the next call names the site she left within two seconds.
why: Killjoy utility only works while she stays near it, so its audio tells you where she is not.

text: When an enemy Operator is holding a lane, do not dry peek it to find out where he is: block his line with a smoke, flash or stun, or locate him with recon first, and if your team has none of that left, take your space on another lane.
when: Deaths to an Operator on a lane where your team still had a smoke, flash or recon unused should be zero.
why: One body or head shot from an Operator kills through heavy armour, so a dry peek hands the holder a free first shot.

text: When you hold an Operator angle and an enemy reveal is coming at you, a recon bolt, an owl drone dart, a Haunt or a stealth drone, shoot it, step out of its sight or let a teammate break it, then come back on a timing or to a different angle, because a revealed Operator is a free kill for the attackers.
when: Rounds where enemy recon tagged you on your Operator angle and you were still on that pixel when they swung.
why: The Operator only wins while the attackers do not know where it is.

text: On a retake, make the attackers' controller an early target when you can reach them, because much of their post plant stall, the smokes and often the mollies, sits in that one kit, and once it is gone the spike is held with guns alone.
when: In retakes you win, count how often the controller died first, and in retakes you lose, how often he was still alive at the defuse.
why: The post plant stall usually comes from one player, so removing him is worth more than any other single kill.

text: When the last defenders still have a controller with a smoke, hold your post plant close to the spike rather than far off site, because a smoke dropped on the spike leaves a far player needing seconds to walk back while they tap.
when: With an enemy smoke still up, your post plant spot is close enough to reach the spike in about two seconds.
why: Distance only works as long as you can see the spike, and a smoke takes that away.

text: As KAY/O on defence, throw the knife onto the choke just as the attackers are about to execute, so they cannot use their utility to support the entry, then fight the lone player who comes in without it.
when: Your knife lands within the last few seconds before the hit, not in the first twenty seconds of the round.
why: A suppressed attack loses its flashes, smokes and recon at the exact moment it needs them.

text: Against players who dive with shotguns, do not stand at the edge of a smoke or walk into the close range they want, hold the smoke from a distance and make them come out to you.
when: Deaths to a shotgun within a few metres of a smoke edge.
why: A shotgun only wins inside its range, so distance turns their dive into a rifle duel they lose.

text: On Raze against a site held behind traps and cameras, clear the setup before anyone walks into it: Paint Shells and an armed Blast Pack destroy destructible sentinel utility such as Cypher trapwires, Killjoy alarmbots and turrets, Deadlock sensors or Vyse razorvine, and the Boom Bot checks a close corner before a body has to.
when: Rounds where the Raze or a teammate walked into an intact trap that an explosive could have cleared.
why: Explosives destroy or trigger the setup before a body has to walk into it.

text: Against a Cypher, locate his setup before you play fast through a smoke: a recon or reveal, a shock or damage ability on the usual wire spots, or a quick jiggle to spot the camera and wires. An entry who runs blind into a set sentinel site gets tethered and revealed and dies for free.
when: Entries that tripped a Cypher trap you had not located.
why: His traps and camera turn speed into a free kill unless they are located first.

text: When the enemy has a site ultimate ready that is strongest on one site, such as a Lockdown or a Viper's Pit, lean toward that site being their goal and treat the open question as when, not where, then plan around it: on defence give that site more weight, on attack against a defending ultimate prefer the other site. It is a lean, not a hard read, because teams fake toward the expected site.

source.topic: enemy site ultimate predicts the site

when: Rounds the enemy used a site ultimate where your team had called that site beforehand.
why: A site ultimate tells you where the enemy wants the fight before the round starts.

text: Against an Iso whose shield is up, remember the shield only eats the first hit, so land one shot to pop it and then change position or re-peek from a new spot, rather than standing still in a long crouched spray whose first and most accurate bullet the shield wasted.
when: Duels against a shielded Iso where you stayed still after the first bullet.
why: His shield blocks one instance of damage, so a burst that assumes it is gone gives him the duel.

text: Against a Hush with Displacement up, do not hold with a wall, a box or a teammate right beside you, because she can burst it on that surface and pull you into it, and only the collision concusses. Give yourself open space or break sight of where it will land.
when: When a Hush pull lands near you, were you within a body of a wall or a teammate.
why: Space around you turns her pull into a move instead of a stun.

text: Against a Chamber who takes a shot and teleports, remember he can only go to his one Rendezvous anchor, so learn where it sits, have a teammate pre aim or pressure that spot right after his shot, and shoot the anchor when you see it, because it is destructible. Since 13.09 the minimap no longer flashes his position after a teleport, so do not wait for it to tell you where he went.
when: After a Chamber teleport, your team checked his anchor spot within a few seconds.
why: His teleport only works inside its range, so the spots he can reach are few and known.

text: When a Chamber holds far forward, especially with an Operator or Headhunter, do not peek him one at a time: swing with two players or behind a flash or stun so his first shot cannot win a free duel, and remember he is far from his teammates, so a kill or a forced teleport there is not traded.
when: Fights against a known forward Chamber where two of you were within trade range.
why: A forward sentinel is strong alone and weak once the fight is traded.

text: When the enemy has a KAY/O, stop running your usual early contest of a main the same way every round, expect the knife there and change the timing or the route, and check his ultimate before you commit utility.

source.topic: enemy KAY/O knife on your contests

when: Rounds where you were suppressed in the same contest twice in a half.
why: A suppression knife on a known contest takes your utility away exactly when you planned to use it.

text: Before you reuse a fast execute against a Vyse, locate or bait her wall and vines first, or hit the other site, because denying a rush through a choke is exactly what her kit does best.
when: Fast hits through a choke into a Vyse site where her wall had not been located.
why: Her setup triggers on the bodies that run through it, so speed alone walks into it.

text: When the enemy comp has no hard flash at all, no Breach, Skye, KAY/O, Phoenix, Yoru, Gekko, Vyse, Hush or Reyna, defend from open long range and high low angles and hold tight to the edge of your smoke, because they cannot blind you off the angle and must walk or dash through to reach you.
when: Against a no flash comp, count rounds you gave up a strong smoke edge before they had shown anything.
why: Without flashes their only way through your hold is movement, which a ready crosshair beats.

text: Against a Yoru, have the player already holding the main his teleport travels through stay quiet and listen for it, because the teleport sound tells your team which side he just left or reached, but he can fake the teleport, so call it as a sound, not a confirmed rotation.
when: Rounds against a Yoru where a teleport sound was called within a second.
why: One listener turns his best rotation tool into information for you.

text: When the attack comes with a Phoenix ultimate, do not take the first duel with him alone: Run it Back returns him to his marker at full health when he takes lethal damage, so your kill only resets him. Back off the angle, play for the second fight when he reappears at the marker, and if his team commits with more utility than you can match, give the space and retake together with your utility and ultimates.

source.topic: enemy Phoenix ultimate on your site

when: Deaths to an ulting Phoenix where you fought him alone.
why: The ultimate makes his first duel free, so the trade comes after it, not during it.

text: Once the spike has less time left than a defuse still needs, seven seconds from the start or three and a half once the half is banked, stop peeking and stay alive, because the defenders can no longer win the round and every fight you take only hands them your gun and an ultimate point.

source.topic: stop peeking when the clock wins

when: Deaths after the spike passed the point where a defuse could still finish.
why: The defuse cannot finish, so any fight you take can only lose the round.

text: When the spike has about ten seconds or less left and the defuser has not reached the half, you do not need to win the duel, you need him off the spike before the half: a kill, or a peek or ability that makes him let go, usually ends the round because a restart needs the full seven seconds again.
when: Late defuses you lost while holding utility that could have stopped them.
why: Interrupting before the half means the defuser needs more time than the spike has.

text: Do not plant while a corner of the site is still uncleared or a fight is still going on behind you, tap the spike to bait a peek and plant only once nobody swings.
when: Deaths while planting with an angle on site still unchecked.
why: The planter has no gun out for four seconds, so an uncleared angle gets a free kill.

text: If you are swung while planting, let go of the plant and take the duel, because a cancelled plant keeps no progress. After the fight, replant only if a full plant still fits in the round time left, otherwise use that time on the next decision.
when: Rounds lost with a cancelled plant and less than four seconds left.
why: A cancelled plant with no time to finish wastes the round.

text: On a retake, group up on the way to the site rather than after the timer has run down, and take the shortest route to the spike when you have the numbers, because a slow regroup forces you to run in late and loud.

source.topic: group on the way, not after

when: Retakes where your team started moving with less than about fifteen seconds of spike left.
why: Time spent regrouping is time the defuse no longer has.

text: As an information initiator, spread your recon across the round, one piece for early control, one for the middle and one kept for the hit or the retake, because spent recon comes back slowly or not at all in the round, and a kit dumped early leaves the commit blind.
when: You still hold one information ability when your team commits to a site or a retake.
why: Information that arrives at the moment of the fight wins it, early information only starts it.

text: A timing peek is a short or crouch peek, show, take the kill and get back so you cannot be traded, and swing wide only on an agent with an escape or in a one versus one.
when: After a timing kill you are back behind cover within about a second.
why: The value of a timing is the surprise, which is gone the moment you stay out.

text: Let the alive count set your risk. When your side is down, look for the isolated fight that can even it. When your side is up, play together, take fights only where a teammate can trade, and do not go hunting a kill alone, though on attack the spike still has to go down.
when: Up in numbers, count deaths to a fight you went looking for.
why: Down numbers you need fights, up numbers the fights are the only way to lose.

text: When a late round becomes two versus one or two versus two with a teammate alive, play off each other, one takes the fight and the other is set to trade within a couple of seconds, instead of taking a solo peek.

source.topic: two versus one as a pair

when: In two player late rounds, deaths where your teammate could not see your killer.
why: A pair that trades turns a coin flip into a won round.

text: As the last defender coming from the far side, get close enough to hear where the spike goes down and where the planter moves, then play the retake off that sound, rather than taking an early fight on the way to find them.

source.topic: last defender stays close enough to hear

when: Rounds you were the last defender and arrived after the plant without knowing where the planter was.
why: Arriving late forces you to clear every corner, while the plant sound tells you where to look.

text: After you win the pistol round, treat the next round as one you must convert, expect the losing side to force and possibly rush, and play it tight and together from range instead of as a free anti eco.

source.topic: the round after a pistol win

when: Bonus rounds lost after a pistol win, and how many of those deaths came alone or inside close range.
why: A lost bonus round hands back the economy and the momentum the pistol earned.

text: If your buys in a half swing between an SMG, a Bulldog and a Sheriff and you rarely hold a rifle with full armour, you are in a force loop, so stop and save with the team so all five buy together next round.
when: Rounds this half you held a rifle with heavy armour, against rounds on a weaker buy.
why: Lone half buys keep the whole team poor without ever winning the round they were bought for.

text: A lost pistol round is not a lost half, so play rounds two and three with the buy the team agrees on, usually a save then a full buy, or a force made together, instead of tilting into a lone force or a hero play.

source.topic: a lost pistol is not a lost half

when: After a lost pistol, rounds two and three are bought as a team.
why: Even at the top level only a small share of halves that start with a lost pistol turn into a stomp.

text: When you are outnumbered with no information, or the spike is down and the retake is lost, save the gun and get out of sight, because the rifle you keep is worth more than a hopeless fight in a round you wanted.

source.topic: save when the round is gone

when: Rifles lost in rounds you were down two or more with no information.
why: The next round needs your gun more than this one needs your death.

text: Every buy phase, read the enemy in the same order, first what they can afford from the last rounds' results and the guns they kept, then the ultimates they have ready, then what they have kept doing this half, and make the plan from that.

source.topic: read the buy phase in a fixed order

when: Before the barrier drops you can say the enemy's likely buy and their ready ultimates.
why: Money decides what they can do, ultimates decide what they will try, habits decide where.

text: Do not spend a round winning ultimate on an enemy eco, keep it for a buy round where it decides a full fight, unless that one ultimate clearly wins the eco on its own.
when: Ultimates used in rounds where the enemy had no rifles.
why: An ultimate thrown at pistols wins a round you were already favoured in.

text: When a dangerous enemy is alive and low on money, play to deny their pickup: name the player who must not get a gun, stand on or hold the dropped rifle or Operator, and make the enemy who goes to pick it up the first target.
when: Rounds the enemy picked up a dropped rifle or Operator and survived with it.
why: A gun that walks away hands their next round a free rifle.

text: When your team holds more ultimates or the better buy, do not take a lone early fight for a pick, use your advantage to win the safe way, and when you are the one behind on money and ultimates, someone, even the controller, has to take the risk.

source.topic: take the risk when you are behind

when: With the better buy, count lone early deaths, with the weaker buy, count rounds nobody took a deliberate risk.
why: The stronger side wins by not giving the round a coin flip, the weaker side wins only by finding one.

text: On the first anti eco after a pistol win, a Guardian held from a long range spot is a strong buy if you can tap accurately, because two body hits kill anyone with light shields or none, so you can fight from where their pistols cannot answer. Against heavy shields it takes three body hits.

source.topic: Guardian on the first anti eco

when: Anti eco deaths inside fifteen metres while you held a long range gun.
why: The anti eco is won at range, and the Guardian kills fastest there against light armour.

text: On defence, keep using the standard one way smokes in ranked, because they make the attackers spend flashes and utility early and give your team an early read on where the hit is going, and wait for the smoke to fully form before you hold through it.
when: Rounds the attackers had to clear your one way with utility before entering.
why: A one way that forces utility buys the rotation time your team needs.

text: When you do not understand why you died or lost a round, save a clip of it straight away and watch it after the match to judge whether the mistake was yours or your team's.
when: One clip saved per match for a moment you could not explain.
why: A short clip of the moment beats a full VOD you never watch.

text: When two of you take the same fight, count it down, three, two, one, and swing in the same moment, with each of you checking a different side, so a single defender cannot take you one at a time.
when: Paired peeks where the second player arrived more than a second after the first.
why: Two players arriving together split the defender's aim, two arriving apart give him two easy duels.

text: When you are the player the enemy is watching, because he just saw you, scanned you or you missed, do not re peek him, keep jiggling to hold his attention while a teammate takes the fight he is not ready for.

source.topic: keep the threat when you are watched

when: After being revealed, count re peeks of the same enemy that died.
why: A defender aimed at you is not aimed at your teammate, and that is the free fight.

text: As the controller on an execute, have your smokes down before the first player enters, then go in right behind the duelist with your gun up to trade, instead of staying at the back placing smokes.
when: On executes, you were within trade range of the entry when the first fight happened.
why: A controller with nothing left to throw is the closest second gun the entry has.

text: As an aggressive player, after a fight or two forward, reset to cover instead of chaining another peek, and with an escape take only one more shot after your opening kill.
when: Deaths on a third consecutive forward peek in the same round.
why: The third forward peek is the one the enemy has had time to prepare for.

text: Expect solo dives onto isolated players to work less the better the lobby gets, because good players are rarely alone, so pair your dive with a teammate who can follow at the same speed.
when: Untraded deaths on a dive with no teammate within a second behind you.
why: A dive needs a lone target, and high level teams do not leave one.

text: After the same execute or setup has run twice against the same team, change one element before the third time, the site, the timing or the utility order, but keep what the enemy recognises so their answer keeps answering the old threat.

source.topic: change one element of a repeated play

when: No set play is run a third time unchanged against the same opponents.
why: A third identical run is read, a small change on a familiar opener is not.

text: Every time the player count changes, say the new numbers first, three versus two, then name it as an advantage or a disadvantage and agree what that means before anyone takes the next fight.
when: After each kill or death, the count is spoken within two seconds.
why: The whole team has to be playing the same situation, and the numbers define it.

text: When you swing or hold with a teammate, say which side you take, I have left, so the other player takes the other side and you never both watch one angle.
when: Paired holds where both of you died to the same side.
why: Two crosshairs on one angle leave the other one free.

text: On defence, beyond the setup you place in the buy phase, spend at most one piece of utility early to spot or slow the likeliest hit and keep the rest for the moment the attackers actually commit, because a recon or molly thrown into a fake or an empty lane is gone when the real push comes.

source.topic: the defender holds utility for the commit

when: Rounds where your stall or recon was spent before the attack showed a commitment.
why: Defensive utility kills when it lands on bodies that have committed.

text: At Ascendant and above, if you play controller and nobody is calling, call some rounds yourself, and if someone else calls, get the plan before the barrier drops, because you decide where the smokes go and a called plan with smokes spent early or late is how calls fail.
when: Rounds a call failed because the smokes were spent or late.
why: The controller already holds the plan in his hands.

text: As the caller, give one plan and keep the team together on it, then let each player decide their own fights inside that plan, and spend your own attention on reading the enemy rather than chasing kills.
when: Calls per round, aim for the plan and the read, not instructions for each duel.
why: A caller who micromanages every move cannot read the next round.

text: Do not make a call, read the minimap and peek at the same moment: make the call from a safe spot first, then give the peek your full attention, and in a pair let the back player read the map while the front player works the crosshair.
when: Deaths while you were mid sentence.
why: Divided attention loses the duel and the call.

text: Choose how wide to swing from who you are swinging on, lower ranked defenders often hold too tight so a wide swing beats them, while higher up you should first recall how that enemy held the angle earlier.
when: Before a committed peek, you can name how that enemy held the angle last time.
why: A swing only works against the hold it was chosen for.

text: Call an empty site as soon as your recon or your watch shows nothing, and as an information initiator send utility to the other site the moment one opens, because the earlier the call, the earlier the rotation lands.
when: Rounds your site was empty and nobody said so before the hit landed elsewhere.
why: Silence on one site is information about the other two.

text: If your mechanics are already good enough for Diamond or Ascendant, stop looking for more aim, review the fights you chose, the re peeks, the untradeable duels and the late utility, because those are what hold you back.
when: In a review, decision deaths outnumber aim deaths, then decisions are the work.
why: Past a point, the duel you should not have taken costs more than the duel you lost.

text: Once you reach Ascendant, plan aim work alongside game sense, because around Immortal most players decide well and mechanics become a bottleneck again: the first accurate shot decides a large share of duels.
when: First bullet hit rate over ten reviewed duels.
why: Everyone at the top decides well, so the first shot separates them.

text: When you hear an enemy run a path, stop and pre aim the next corner he must clear on it, because footsteps tell you both where he is and where he is about to look.

source.topic: pre aim the corner he must clear

when: After hearing steps, your crosshair was already on the corner he came out of.
why: You get to be ready on the spot he has to check first.

text: When an enemy you spotted can come back from the same spot or from a second exit, keep your crosshair where you saw him until he could have walked to the other exit, and only then treat it as a guess.

source.topic: hold until he could have moved

when: Deaths to an enemy re peeking the spot you had just looked away from.
why: For the first seconds the same edge is not a guess, it is the likeliest spot.

text: Inside the agents you already play well, pick the role for the session by how your aim feels in the warm up, an entry duelist on a day you are hitting shots, a sentinel or initiator on a day you are not, so you still help through utility when the duels are not landing.

source.topic: role by how your aim feels

when: On an off day, at least one utility role pick.
why: Utility works on bad aim days, entry duels do not.

text: From Iron to Gold, put most of your practice into aim, crosshair placement, movement and deathmatch rather than strategy, because there is little coordination at those ranks and your own duels carry you out.
when: Most of your practice time in deathmatch until you leave Gold.
why: Team plans need teammates who follow them, mechanics only need you.

text: If you spray first and correct after, practise with the Sheriff or the Guardian for a while, because those guns punish anything but a stopped, aimed first shot.
when: One deathmatch per session with a one tap gun.
why: A gun that cannot spray teaches the first shot.

text: When you change a mechanic, use it in every ranked fight even when the old habit would win that one fight, and expect to play worse for a stretch before it pays.
when: The new mechanic is used in every duel for a full week of games.
why: A habit only forms if it is used under pressure.

text: If you cannot spot your own mistakes yet, watch one replay with someone at least a few ranks above you and copy what they pick on.
when: One replay a week reviewed with a stronger player.
why: A player above you sees the decisions you do not know are decisions.

text: When you lead near the end of a map, or in overtime, play the simple, practised rounds that built the lead, and expect the trailing team to rush and force, so slow down, keep your structure and treat every round, anti ecos included, at full attention instead of gambling to finish.
when: At match point, rounds run with an untested plan.
why: Leads are thrown by new ideas and early solo aggression.

text: Place an execute smoke so that a defender leaving it has one predictable edge to come out of, because a smoke he can leave from either side breaks your crosshair placement on every exit.

source.topic: place smokes for a predictable exit

when: Your smokes on an execute leave at most one exit toward your team.
why: You decide where his face appears.

text: When you lurk, do not take even fifty fifty duels, spend utility or wait for information so the fight you take is already tilted your way, because a lost lurk fight leaves your team a player down for nothing.

source.topic: a lurker never takes even duels

when: Lurk deaths in a duel you started without any edge.
why: A lurker's whole value is the surprise, which an even duel throws away.

text: As the Operator player, staying alive is itself map pressure, so after an early kill keep holding or reposition with your escape ready instead of trading your gun for a forward peek.
when: Operators lost on a second peek after an opening kill.
why: Holding still already freezes the enemy, peeking forward only risks the gun.

text: In agent select, name what the enemy comp lacks, hard flashes, a dive or crossing tool, a site stalling sentinel, an Operator player, and say it aloud, because each missing tool is a play that will keep working against them.

source.topic: read what the enemy comp lacks

when: Before round one, one sentence on what the enemy comp cannot do.
why: The comp tells you which plans they cannot answer before round one.

text: Shape your Viper wall so it keeps value through the round, a first line, a half site hold, then the retake, instead of a wall that only blocks the first choke and is then ignored.

source.topic: a Viper wall with several phases

when: In a round, how many separate parts of your wall your team used.
why: Most of a wall that covers only the first choke is wasted length.

text: As a duelist with your ultimate up, do not spend it on an early isolated duel away from the plan: take the area in steps with a teammate's dart, drone or flash for the next corner, and use the ultimate as part of the site take or the fight that decides the round.

source.topic: take space in steps before the ultimate

when: Ultimate rounds where you used it before reaching the site.
why: An ultimate spent on the first corner is gone for the fight that matters.

text: As Astra, keep one star unplaced or ready to move for a fast request or for wherever the hit goes, instead of committing all of them at round start.
when: At the start of each round one star is still flexible.
why: A star already placed on the wrong site is a smoke you do not have.

text: As a defending Yoru, play an aggressive line only with a Gatecrash already placed behind you, take one shot, then teleport out to reset or rotate, and if you still hold a charge, set it toward the other site again.

source.topic: Yoru defence with a Gatecrash behind you

when: Aggressive Yoru deaths with no Gatecrash placed.
why: The teleport turns a one and done aggression into a safe one, but it only resets every two kills.

text: As a sentinel on attack, stay off entry duty, hold the gap your teammates are not looking at and turn to the flank once the last one passes you, unless a trap already watches the flank, because if you enter and die the flank watch and the post plant die with you.

source.topic: the sentinel on attack watches the back

when: Attack rounds you died first or second as the sentinel.
why: The sentinel's kit is built for the half of the round after the entry.

text: If you get many kills and still lose, sort them by timing: opening kills and kills on site during a hit, retake or post plant decide rounds, while lurk kills on a lost round, kills on rotating players and exit kills after the round is decided rarely change the result. Exit kills still cost the enemy a saved gun, so they help the economy, not the round.

source.topic: judge kills by when they happened

when: In a review, opening and site kills against kills after the round was decided.
why: Kill count hides whether the kills won anything.

text: After a rush wins against you, expect the same rush again and prepare your damage utility for it, and after you shut a hit down completely, expect the next round to go elsewhere and lean your setup that way.
when: The round after a lost rush, your utility was ready on that entrance.
why: Teams repeat what worked and abandon what failed.

text: Take a solo push or lane timing only while your team has pulled the enemy's attention somewhere else, because alone with no pressure anywhere you are simply being held.

source.topic: a solo push only under pressure

when: Solo timing deaths while no teammate was in contact.
why: A timing works when the defender is looking away.

text: In an even fight late in the round with the spike not yet planted, four versus four or three versus three, a defence split two and two across sites meets the hit with half its players, so regroup toward one side or the middle, leave utility or one watcher for information on the other site, and be ready to retake it together.
when: Late even rounds where the hit met two or fewer defenders.
why: The attack chooses one site, a split defence meets it with half.

text: Make noise on purpose and only on purpose, when a teammate is lined up on a defender make a sound from a different angle so he turns, and when you are the quiet one, walk silently looking for the punish.
when: Every loud action in a round is one the team chose.
why: A defender can only face one sound at a time.

text: On a hit that depends on surprise, walk and do not reload, switch weapons or jump until the hit goes, because one noise hands the defenders the timing. Walking costs time, so do it when the round clock allows.
when: Rounds a surprise route was heard before contact.
why: The player who hears you is always more ready than you are.

text: When you hug cover, stand slightly back from the edge rather than pressed against it, because an arm or a foot can stick out to an enemy angling you while you cannot see him.
when: Deaths to a shot from an angle you thought you were hidden from.
why: Being seen first by a sliver is still being seen first.

text: Set each session's goal as one skill to improve, not a rank to reach, because a player chasing rank keeps playing the way that put them there.
when: One named skill written before each session.
why: A process goal changes how you play, a rank goal only changes how you feel.

text: When the defence matches you everywhere or goes quiet after an early kill, create a visible threat on one area with a little utility, let them lean toward it, then hit the other area hard while they are still leaning.

source.topic: show a threat then hit the other area

when: After a show of pressure, the hit lands within about fifteen seconds.
why: A defence that reacts to every threat can be moved by one.

text: Track the enemy team's repeated rules, where and when their first smoke goes, how they answer a default, what makes their rotator move, because a team that answers the same way every round can be planned against.
when: By the middle of a half you can state one if then rule the enemy has shown twice.
why: Most teams change positions more than they change their rules.

text: Track one enemy player's habit across rounds, the same off angle, the same early push, the gun he always buys, because most ranked players do not change how they play during a game.
when: One enemy habit named by the middle of the first half.
why: A habit seen twice is a position you can pre aim the third time.

text: When defence goes a player down early, call to stabilise, stop taking new duels, concede the site your plan says is easiest to retake and keep two together in each remaining zone.

source.topic: stabilise a man down on defence

when: Early man down rounds where a new duel was taken alone in the next ten seconds.
why: Four spread players cover the map, four paired players win fights.

text: To climb from Ascendant into Immortal, cut the deaths where you are picked alone in the opening and the mid round, because at that level an untraded death decides more rounds than any duel you win.
when: Untraded deaths before the first teammate death or before the plant, brought down match over match.
why: The team that loses fewer free players wins the even rounds.

text: If you are stuck in Silver or Gold, look first for ego fights, overaggression, playing apart from the team and wasted utility, before you blame your aim.
when: In one match, tag each death as ego peek, overextension, isolated or utility misuse.
why: Those habits cost more rounds at that rank than missed shots.

text: Call every enemy you see with the place and the count, and anything you spot of their utility, so whatever plan your team runs is working from the real picture.
when: Every contact called with location and count.
why: A plan only works on the information it is fed.

text: By Gold, narrow to one or two agents and learn them deeply, their lineups and their setups on each map, while staying able to fill one agent in each other role.
when: Distinct agents in your last twenty matches, more than three is too wide.
why: Depth on one agent wins more than five agents played at half value.

text: Run executes with the abilities in order, smokes down, then the flash or reveal, then the entry crossing within about a second of the pop, rather than each player using abilities on their own time.
when: The entry crosses the site line within about a second of the flash or reveal popping.
why: Utility that lands together wins the site, utility that lands apart is cleared piece by piece.

text: From Diamond up, check in agent select that the team has a controller with smokes, and if nobody else will play one, fill it yourself rather than adding another duelist.
when: Rounds played with zero controllers on your team.
why: A team with no smokes cannot take or hold a site against coordinated players.

text: Once your sentinel setup or defensive start has been seen, vary it, move the trap, the cage or the corner you hold, and keep two or three setups per site, because conditioning the enemy is a large part of defence at high rank.

source.topic: vary your setup once it is seen

when: Across a half, your setup on a site changes at least once after it has been seen.
why: A setup the attackers have already solved is a setup they will pre clear.

text: Outfragging a low rank lobby is not proof you are underranked, rank follows wins far more than kills, so review your deaths for crosshair placement and positioning rather than waiting for the rank to catch up.
when: Win rate over the last twenty games and one reviewed game per session.
why: Kills in a lost game do not move the rank the way wins do.

text: At low rank, do not build your game around long range damage lineups. Take more fights on the site with your team, and in the post plant play close enough to be traded, using your molly or shock dart to stop the defuse or block one choke while you fight beside them.
when: Rounds you threw a lineup from a spot no teammate could trade you from.
why: Your team needs your gun on the site more than a lineup from far away.

text: Keep your movement ability for the entry itself: a duelist who spends the dash, slide or satchel early has nothing to enter with and nothing to survive on site with.

source.topic: keep your dash for the entry

when: Your movement ability is still available at the moment of the execute.
why: The dash is the entry, using it to look around wastes it.

text: Up to Gold, move with a teammate and stay close enough that if the player ahead of you dies you can shoot the killer within a second or two.
when: For each teammate death near you, did the killer die within about three seconds.
why: Distance is what turns a death into a trade.

text: When you are down numbers on attack, make no sound until you fight, while the timer allows it, because silence forces the defenders to cover every gap you could come through and sooner or later one of them moves into your timing. Watch the clock, the spike still has to be planted.
when: Outnumbered rounds where you were heard before your first shot.
why: A quiet player is a threat in every lane at once.

text: When the full hit lands on you alone, take a pick only if it is cheap, then fall back toward your team and live for the retake, because your second job is to draw utility and crosshairs while the others flood.

source.topic: fall back from the lone hit, cheaply

when: Rounds you died alone on a hit site with no kill and no utility thrown.
why: One live defender on the retake is worth more than one kill and a death.

text: When your entry dies early on attack and you are four against five, do not give up the round, group up, agree one plan and either trade the count back with picks or hit one site together.
when: Four versus five rounds where the remaining players split across the map.
why: Four players on one site still outnumber the defenders there.

text: Pair an ability that holds an enemy in place with damage on the same spot, a slow, a tether or a net followed by a molly or a grenade, and if you queue as a duo, plan that combo so the initiator sets up the duelist every round.
when: Rounds your damage utility landed on an enemy your teammate had just held in place.
why: A player who cannot walk out of the damage takes all of it.

text: On a retake, wait for your teammate's flash or reveal to land and swing on it with the next player on a count, never before it, unless the spike timer no longer leaves time for the utility and the defuse.
when: Retake deaths that came before your team's reveal or flash popped.
why: A retake that swings early fights a planted team with full information.
