text: On an anti eco, clear the close corners first from range and fight down long lines, walk together, keep reloaded and never wander alone into a site, because a lone death hands the saving team a rifle.
when: Anti eco deaths inside about ten metres or with no teammate in trade range.
why: The eco only wins in the close fights and with the gun you give them.

text: Take ultimate orbs that sit on your safe path at round start, but never walk into a contested spot for an orb in a round you cannot afford to lose, and never while your teammates are fighting on site.
when: Deaths within a few seconds of picking up or heading to an orb.
why: An orb is worth a round only if it does not cost a player.

text: Keep a smoke you do not need yet instead of throwing it onto an area nobody is contesting, say that you are holding it, and on a site that is falling keep one for after the plant.

source.topic: keep a smoke you do not need yet

when: Rounds you ended with no smoke while a smoke went on an uncontested area earlier.
why: An unused smoke is a retake or a stuck teammate saved.

text: In agent select, if a teammate only plays one agent, give them that agent and fill the missing role from your pool, and ask who is comfortable on what rather than forcing anyone onto an agent.

source.topic: fill without a fight in agent select

when: Matches with an argument in agent select.
why: A team where each player is on a comfortable agent plays better than a perfect comp on paper.

text: After a round you should have won is lost to a clutch or a teammate's mistake, say something supportive, call a reset in the buy phase and run the plan you came in with, instead of blaming or changing style.
when: Next rounds after a thrown round where the team stayed on the plan.
why: The next round is lost when the team carries the last one into it.

text: When a solo queue team ignores every plan, find the one teammate who is clearly trying, agree a plan with them, then ask one named player to join the two of you, because people follow a plan that already has two players.

source.topic: when your team will not follow

when: Rounds you called with a partner who agreed first.
why: Two committed players make a plan visible to the rest.

text: On a site hit, do not send all five onto the site: one player, often the sentinel or the controller, stays in main or a flank lane to watch the retake path and build a crossfire for the post plant.

source.topic: sentinel stays in main on the hit

when: Executes where all five ended up on site.
why: A planted site with one player behind the retake path is far harder to take back.

text: On a retake or an entry, cross as your initiator's flash or blind pops, never before it and not long after it has worn off.

source.topic: commit on the flash, not before

when: Entries and retakes where you crossed before the flash popped.
why: A swing before the flash fights a defender who can see.

text: When your recon on a site shows nothing and teammates hold mid, leave that site to its sentinel setup and rotate the flexible player to the site with the fewest defenders, so no site is left on one body when a split or a hit lands.
when: After an empty site scan, the flex player moved within ten seconds.
why: The setup can hold an empty site, a body cannot hold two.

text: When you clear an area and leave it to hit the other site, put one more smoke there, keep a player or leave a trap, so the defenders cannot confirm it is empty and rotate for free.

source.topic: leave a sign on the area you leave

when: Hits where the defence rotated after checking the area you had left.
why: An area they can check freely tells them where you went.

text: Do not let one enemy Operator stop your whole attack, it can hold only one lane at a time, so locate it with information and keep taking your space and peeks on the lanes it is not on.

source.topic: an Operator lane is one lane

when: Rounds your team took no space anywhere after one Operator kill.
why: A frozen team gives the Operator the round without a shot.

text: Count the enemy's spent smokes, flashes and recon out loud as the round goes, and once a type is gone, take the fight it would have stopped before it can come back.
when: Fights taken within a few seconds of an enemy smoke or flash being called spent.
why: Most spent utility is gone for the round, and a signature ability only comes back after its cooldown, so the window is now.

text: As a lurker, know the moment your team commits to a site and either arrive with them or hold your post plant utility for that site, because a lurk still on the far side when the team hits is wasted.
when: Hits where the lurker arrived after the plant or not at all.
why: The lurk exists to help the hit, not to run beside it.

text: If you take two areas at once and nobody contests either, read the defenders as stacked in the remaining areas, and if utility from three different agents comes from one place, count three players there and hit elsewhere.
when: After two uncontested areas, the hit avoided the remaining one.
why: What the defence does not contest tells you where it is.

text: Before you hold a deep early position on defence, ask whether a teammate can trade you if the attackers come with two players or utility, and if nobody can, play it only on an agent that can escape or leave after one shot.

source.topic: hold the deep line only with an exit

when: Deaths on a deep spot with no escape used and no trade.
why: A deep spot that can be pinched from two sides is one kill at best.

text: Against a defending Chamber who wants the first duel, send utility down his lane before you walk it, a drone, a Prowler or a Haunt, so he has to spend time and shots breaking it or gets revealed before he can take his shot.
when: Opening deaths to a Chamber on a lane you sent no utility into.
why: Utility makes his first shot cost a teammate.

text: When you find the enemy sentinel's setup, a Cypher camera, a Killjoy turret or a Vyse Razorvine, work out the rest of the defence from it: if the sentinel and the controller are both on one site, the other site has fewer players, so hit the weak site or split around it.
when: After locating a sentinel setup, the next hit went to the other site.
why: A sentinel's setup shows where the rest of the team is not.

text: If the defence's opening utility tells you their mid player sits passive, take mid with numbers and force the fight on the lone mid player before committing to a site.

source.topic: a defender who matches with numbers

when: Rounds you took mid with two or more when it showed one passive defender.
why: A passive lone mid player is the cheapest kill on the map.

text: As Gekko, send your creatures early for information and pick the globules back up, and throw Dizzy high when you expect it to be shot so the globule falls near you. Only reclaim from a spot no enemy can see, because the reclaim takes time and a globule left too long expires.
when: Rounds you reclaimed at least one creature.
why: A reclaimed creature is the same ability twice in one round.

text: On attack against an eco, smoke the deep angles such as heaven and the defenders' rotation spots rather than smoking right on top of them, and fight the rest at range, because a close smoke forces the close fight their pistols win.
when: Anti eco smokes placed on top of close defender spots.
why: Your rifles want distance, so your smokes should remove only the angles that deny it.

text: On an attacking eco, move as a group of four or five and swing together, so the first kill can be traded and a rifle picked up, with the weaker pistols going in first for the Sheriffs behind them.
when: Eco rounds where your team took its first fight with nobody close enough to trade.
why: Five pistols together trade, five pistols apart are five free rifle kills.

text: When an execute is too heavy to hold, let the site go and retake from at least three directions, the players from other areas coming through the middle or the far side, timed to arrive together, rather than only from spawn and one entrance.
when: Retakes where all your players came through the same one or two entrances.
why: A post plant can watch two entrances, not three.

text: Before you swing onto a site, throw a molly into the tight spot a defender tucks into and onto any likely trap spot, then follow with your own flash or a teammate's, because the molly forces him to stand wider where the flash and your swing catch him.

source.topic: molly the tuck spot, then flash

when: Site entries where your molly and flash landed on the same defender spot.
why: A tucked defender beats a flash by turning away, a burning one has to move first.

text: In solo queue and in rank up games, play an agent you have many recent games on, and do not instalock a specialist such as Astra, Harbor, Viper or Yoru unless you have practised it, because their value comes from practised setups and timings.
when: Ranked games on an agent you played fewer than about ten times before.
why: A comfortable agent keeps your fundamentals, a new one takes your attention away from them.

text: As a lurker, sit at an insert spot near the enemy rotation path and listen, and when you hear them run or teleport away to answer your team, either call the swap or take a fast wide timing peek on the rotators as they pass.

source.topic: the lurker listens for the rotate

when: Lurk rounds where you heard a rotation and acted on it within a few seconds.
why: A rotation is the moment the defence turns its back on you.

text: On a retake as the controller, direct the traffic, first hold everyone, then say what utility you will use and where, then count down and call go as it lands.
when: Retakes where the team entered on your count.
why: The smokes decide when the retake can start, so the player throwing them should time it.

text: Against a Fade, shoot her Prowler or put a pillar, a pole or a corner between you and it before it locks on, because it chases the first enemy it sees, and once it is biting it keeps tracking you.
when: Prowler hits taken while cover was a step away.
why: A prowler that cannot see you cannot nearsight you.

text: As a site anchor, your first job is to stay alive and delay, so judge the hold by the seconds you bought, because even five more seconds lets rotators arrive with utility and a round with no kills but a long delay is a successful hold.
when: Seconds from first contact on your site to the plant, longer is the goal.
why: Nobody wins one versus two consistently, the anchor wins rounds by making the retake possible.

text: Before you blame your aim for lost duels, check your setup: a high refresh monitor, around 144 Hz, with a frame rate that stays high in fights, makes moving targets easier to track and is common among players above Platinum.
when: Monitor refresh rate and in game frame rate during fights.
why: Every frame you do not see is a frame the enemy already moved in.

text: Pick one moderate sensitivity that suits your own setup and keep it for weeks, instead of changing it often or copying another player, because flick distance only becomes muscle memory while it stays the same.
when: Days since your last sensitivity change, aim for weeks.
why: A setting changed every week resets the habit every week.

text: When an early recon dart is going to be broken anyway, throw it where your duelists can see the shot or where only the deeper, safer defender can reach it, so the tracer of whoever breaks it tells your team where one enemy is.

source.topic: a dart that will be broken

when: Early darts broken with nobody on your team watching the break.
why: A broken dart still gives information if someone is watching who breaks it.

text: Use an aim trainer for raw crosshair control, where you fire thousands of shots in a short time, and use deathmatch and real angles for crosshair placement, angle switching and movement, which a trainer cannot teach.
when: Each practice block names whether it trains control or placement.
why: Placement is learned on the maps you play, control is learned by repetition.

text: On attack Tailwind is how you enter a site, not something to keep for later: throw Cloudburst where you will land and dash into it as a teammate's flash, dart or drone lands, because walking or swinging onto the site with the dash unused throws away the one thing that makes your entry safer than anyone else's.
when: Attack rounds where the Jett died entering a site with Tailwind still available.
why: Every vetted entry source teaches the dash as the entry, and a dash kept for later is why a Jett entry dies like anyone else.

text: When your initiator's drone, dog or dart reveals a defender or shows the first angle clear, enter in that same second, onto the revealed player while he is still where it saw him, with the next teammate taking the next angle behind you, because a reveal is worth most the moment it lands and a defender who knows he was seen moves.
when: Entries that came seconds after a teammate recon had already landed, or before it landed.
why: Entering on the information is what the entry controls, and it is the part the old trade advice never said.

text: When the defence dumps mollies, stuns or a wall on the entrance you are about to satchel through, do not fly into it: pull back, let the utility run out and hit after it is spent or take another route, because a satchel into fresh defensive utility gives the round away and they cannot throw that utility twice.
when: Raze deaths on landing inside a molly, stun or wall the defence threw seconds earlier.
why: The one case where an entry should wait is fresh stall utility on the entrance.

text: On defence keep Paint Shells until the attackers commit, then throw them into the entrance behind the first player through, so the group behind him is held back while you and your team kill the one who came in, because a rush only works when everyone arrives together.
when: Defence rounds lost to a rush with the Raze grenade unused or thrown before contact.
why: The grenade in the doorway splits the rush, which is the whole point of holding it.

text: As a defending Jett, take an early aggressive peek only with Tailwind prepared before you show yourself, then take one fight and dash out, because Tailwind resets only every two kills, so a dash spent getting to the peek leaves you no way out of it.
when: Early defence deaths on a forward peek with Tailwind unavailable or unprepared.
why: Pros do take early defence space, never without the exit. Split from one card for four duelists (round 3 audit, after2): it named every duelist's exit to each of them and said all of them come back on two kills, which the 13.09 kit says of Tailwind, the slide and Gatecrash but not of Blast Pack.

text: As a defending Neon, take an early aggressive peek only with the slide ready before you show yourself, then take one fight and slide out, because the High Gear slide resets only every two kills, so a slide spent getting to the peek leaves you no way out of it.
when: Early defence deaths on a forward peek with the slide already spent.
why: Pros do take early defence space, never without the exit, and the 13.09 kit resets the High Gear slide every two kills.

text: As a defending Yoru, take an early aggressive peek only with Gatecrash placed behind you just before you show yourself, then take one fight and teleport out, because Gatecrash resets only every two kills, so a teleport spent getting to the peek is not there to leave it.
when: Early defence deaths on a forward peek with no Gatecrash placed behind.
why: Pros do take early defence space, never without the exit, and the 13.09 kit resets Gatecrash every two kills. The card says nothing of charges, which the game data does not carry.

text: As a defending Raze, take an early aggressive peek only with a Blast Pack in hand to jump out before you show yourself, then take one fight and leave, because Blast Pack does not reset on kills the way Paint Shells does, so a satchel spent getting to the peek is one fewer way out for the rest of the round.
when: Early defence deaths on a forward peek with the satchels already spent.
why: Pros do take early defence space, never without the exit. In the 13.09 kit Paint Shells resets every two kills and Blast Pack does not, so the old shared card's two kill line was false for a Raze.

text: You have no dash or slide on Iso, so advice to peek and dash away does not fit you: take early peeks one step from cover with Double Tap up, since its shield blocks one hit, and fall back on foot right after the first fight instead of staying for a second.
when: Iso deaths on a second fight from the same forward spot.
why: Generic duelist exit advice assumes a movement ability Iso does not have.

text: On Reyna, Dismiss and Devour need a Soul Orb, and an orb appears only when an enemy you damaged or killed is dead, so take your first defensive peek from a spot one step from cover that you can survive with no ability, and never go into a lane where you know three attackers are.
when: Reyna deaths on a first wide defensive peek before any orb existed.
why: Low rank Reyna players peek as if the escape already existed.

text: When a Cypher Trapwire covers the line you would dash along, do not dash through it: Updraft and dash over it, ask an initiator to break it first, or land on another spot, because a trip holds you in the open with your dash already spent.
when: Jett deaths tethered on the dash line into a site.
why: A trip on the usual dash line turns the fastest entry into the most exposed one.

text: With Blade Storm out throw single knives with fire, which refresh on every kill, and keep the alt fire throw of all remaining knives for an enemy right on top of you, because that throw spends every knife with no refresh.
when: Blade Storm rounds that ended with the knives spent on one spread throw.
why: The kit refreshes single throws on kills and not the spread throw.

text: On the pistol round an enemy holding a Ghost, a Frenzy, a Bandit or a Sheriff almost certainly bought no shield, because every bought pistol plus any shield costs more than the 800 you start with, so a Ghost inside 30 metres, a Bandit or a Sheriff kills him with one head hit and a Classic needs a second, which is why you keep tapping until he drops.
when: Pistol round duels where the player stopped firing after one head hit.
why: His gun tells you his armour, and his armour tells you how many hits he needs.

text: On an anti eco a Bandit head hit kills through Heavy Armor only inside 10 metres, but a Sheriff head hit kills through it out to 30 metres and a Marshal head hit at any range, so meet close corners from distance or clear them with utility, and never give a Sheriff or a Marshal a still head on a long line.
when: Anti eco deaths to a Bandit up close or to a Sheriff or Marshal on a long line.
why: Each cheap gun has one range where it equals a rifle, and it is a different range for each.

text: If a Classic killed you on an anti eco, you were usually already hurt or within a few metres of him, because one Classic head hit does not kill even a player with no shield, so check your health before the next fight and clear close corners with utility instead of walking into them.
when: Anti eco deaths to a Classic.
why: A Classic death is one of the most readable deaths in the game.

text: When the buy phase shows three or more enemies on Light Armor, an Outlaw held on a long angle kills each of them with one body hit for about half an Operator's price, so it can be a better buy than a rifle that round, but against Heavy Armor it needs a second hit.
when: Buy rounds against three or more light shields where the long angle player bought a rifle.
why: One body hit kills a light shield, so the gun plays like an Operator against most of that team.

text: When an enemy Omen uses From the Shadows near you, look for the shade at the spot he is going to arrive and shoot it, because the shade can be destroyed and that stops his arrival, and if you cannot find it, hold that spot instead of turning your back on it.
when: Deaths to an Omen just arrived from his ultimate.
why: The kit makes the shade destructible, and a destroyed shade sends him back.

text: Against an Omen, listen for the short channel of Shrouded Step: when you hear it close to you, turn to the nearest spot he could land and aim there instead of keeping your crosshair on the angle you were holding, because the teleport puts him beside or behind you a moment later.
when: Deaths to an Omen from behind or above shortly after a teleport sound.
why: The step has a channel and its enemy audio was made clearer in 13.00.

text: When an Omen's Paranoia reaches you, you are nearsighted and deafened, so step back behind cover or toward a teammate until it wears off instead of holding the doorway half blind, because he throws it to swing you while you cannot see or hear him.
when: Deaths while nearsighted by Paranoia on the same angle.
why: Paranoia nearsights and deafens, it is not a smoke and it is not a flash you can turn from.

text: When a Reyna throws Leer at your angle, shoot it or look away from it and keep your position, because it nearsights only players looking at it and it can be destroyed, so holding your angle while staring into it hands her the duel.
when: Deaths to a Reyna swinging behind her Leer.
why: Leer only works on a player who keeps looking at it.

text: Do not chase a Reyna who Dismisses after a kill, because for that moment she cannot be hurt and she is moving back to cover you cannot see, so hold the way back to you and make her come to you.
when: Deaths chasing a Reyna who just vanished with Dismiss.
why: Chasing walks you into the angle she chose while she is already safe.

text: Fight a Reyna with a teammate who swings at the same moment from a second angle, never one after the other, because each enemy she kills gives her an orb to heal or Dismiss, so two duels in a row are two she can reset between.
when: Two deaths in a row to the same Reyna in one round.
why: Her whole kit runs on orbs from players she killed.

text: When a Killjoy Alarmbot reaches you it makes you vulnerable, so you take extra damage, and it does not slow you: shoot it if it is right beside you, otherwise step straight back out of the entrance and come in again with a teammate, because the next step forward is where her swarm and turret are waiting.
when: Entry deaths with the Alarmbot debuff on.
why: The coach once called the Alarmbot a slow and swapped the keys, the kit says vulnerable.

text: When a Killjoy Lockdown goes down over you, shoot the device during its windup if you can see it from cover, otherwise walk out of the circle before it goes off and come back when it ends, and do not leave it through a lane the enemy is holding.
when: Deaths detained inside a Lockdown.
why: The device is destructible and only detains after a delay, so the windup is the whole answer.

text: Shoot a Sage wall the moment it goes up, before it fortifies, and break more of it than you need to pass so no corner is left to hide behind, then check the top of what is left, because Sages often stand on their own walls.
when: Executes stalled behind a Sage wall or deaths to a player on top of one.
why: The wall fortifies after a delay, so the first seconds are the cheap ones.

text: Do not run through a Sage slow to keep moving, because it slows you and plays a sound to her team as you cross it, so wait it out or go around its edge, and if half your team is caught in it on an execute, stop and regroup instead of feeding the rest through.
when: Execute deaths inside a Sage slow.
why: Crossing the slow announces you as well as slowing you.

text: When a Phoenix Curveball bends around a corner toward you, turn away until it pops, then turn straight back to that corner, because at lower ranks the Phoenix swings right behind his flash, and it comes back every two kills, so expect another from a Phoenix on a streak.
when: Deaths to a Phoenix swinging off his own flash.
why: The flash curves and pops after a delay, which gives you the turn.

text: Do not take a duel with a Phoenix standing in his own Blaze or Hot Hands fire, because it heals him while it burns you, so back off until it dies down or make him leave it first.
when: Duels lost against a Phoenix inside his fire.
why: Inner Fire heals him in his own fire and the fire damages everyone else.

text: When you kill a Phoenix during Run it Back he is not dead, he returns to his marker with full health, so do not walk forward or reload in the open after that kill: move to a new spot and expect him again from where he started the ultimate.
when: Deaths to a Phoenix a few seconds after killing his ultimate copy.
why: The plat and up note covers the team answer, this is the low band version.

text: Right after a Clove gets a kill, do not take an even duel with her alone, because Pick-me-up on the body gives her haste and overheal, so trade her with a second player at once or back off until it wears off.
when: Deaths to a Clove just after she took a kill.
why: The kit turns her kill into extra health and speed for the next duel.

text: If a Chamber Trademark slows you at a choke, back out of the slow instead of walking on or swinging while slowed, because a trapped choke is usually one he or a teammate is watching, and break it from outside or go in together once it is gone.
when: Deaths while slowed by a Trademark at an entrance.
why: A slowed player at a watched choke is the easiest kill on the map.

text: Do not treat a lost retake as a mistake by itself, because even the best professional teams lose more retakes than they win: judge it by whether it should have been played at all and how you entered it, together or one at a time.
when: Reviews that blame a lost retake on the result alone.
why: Outcome bias: the decision and the entry are what the player controls.

text: On the way to a retake say in one line what utility you have, then go in at the same moment as the teammate nearest you, one of you on the spike behind a smoke or a wall while the other fights, and if nobody answers, follow the closest teammate in rather than entering alone.
when: Low band retakes entered one player at a time.
why: The low band retake notes were geometry, this is the version that survives a silent lobby.

text: When the spike goes down while a teammate is still alive on or beside the site, go to him now and fight beside him instead of backing off to set up a later retake, because a retake that starts with one player already inside is easier than any you can set up after he dies alone.
when: Post plant deaths of a defender still on site while rotators waited outside.
why: A live teammate inside is a free extra angle that disappears in seconds.

text: When your attack keeps losing rounds with players spread one here, three there, one there, stop spreading: start four or five together, move in pairs at the very least and commit to one site with the utility you have for it, because a split nobody commits to lets the defence beat each part on its own.
when: A run of lost attack rounds with deaths spread across the map.
why: In both sources the close rounds were the committed ones and the blowouts the spread ones.

text: Work on one named habit at a time and keep it for a few days of games before you add another, judging each game by whether you did it, because a few games played with one thing to fix improve you far more than many games played trying to fix everything.
when: Practice and climb questions.
why: Two independent sources give the same method in different words.

text: If you only have about twenty minutes a day, do them every day, a few minutes of Range bots from easy to hard and one or two deathmatches with one focus, because a short routine kept daily does far more than one long session a week.
when: Practice questions from players with little time.
why: A routine the player cannot keep is worth nothing.

text: Trading cannot be practised alone, deathmatch has no teammates, so drill the solo half there, peeking one spot at a time from further off the wall so only one enemy can see you, and practise the team half in your matches with one glance at the minimap for your nearest teammate before each swing.
when: Practice questions from a player whose counted mistake is untraded deaths.
why: The coach invented a deathmatch drill that needs teammates, this is the doable version.

text: From high Ascendant up, aim is rarely what separates you from the next level unless your own deaths show lost even duels, the gap is decisions: play the economy and ultimates, read the enemy's habits and call on them, plan the post plant before you reach the site, and practise that structure in Premier with a fixed group.
when: Climb questions at Ascendant and up.
why: Two independent high level sources agree the top gap is structure, with the caveat that a weak earlier layer comes first.

text: Do not judge your aim by your headshot rate alone, because it barely tracks how well even professionals play and it drops for reasons that are not aim, spraying through smokes, wallbanging and fights with shotguns, machine guns or snipers.
when: Aim questions answered from the headshot rate.
why: Across professional players the rate sits in a wide band and barely correlates with their rating.

text: On Split attack in a gun round, do not run all five through one main: fight for mid or a ramp with utility first, then slow down and choose the site, and keep the five player rush for pistol and eco rounds.
when: Split attack rounds lost with five players in one main.
why: Two vetted coaches agree, and Split is out of the ranked pool since 13.08, so this reaches unrated and swiftplay only.

text: On Split plant where your teammates can see the spike from outside the site, use the sheltered default corner only when you have no time, and then move one player off site to play the post plant from there.
when: Split post plants lost with everyone crowded on the site.
why: Two vetted coaches give the same open plant versus safe plant trade.

text: On Corrode do not plan an A post plant from A Link, and expect defenders to reach the back of both sites sooner than older guides say, because since 13.08 the A plant zone and the defender paths were changed for exactly that.
when: Corrode A post plants played from A Link.
why: Riot changed both on purpose, and the guides written before it say the opposite.
